IGNITION The warning light is event-driven (fault onset) by a command from the NBC The warning light may come on with a fixed or flashing light according to NBC status (see CODE system operation) SWITCHING OFF The warning light is turned up when a command is received from the NBC or if the NQS is disconnected from the B-CAN network. Glow plug preheating (only for jtd engine) The information is displayed by means of a symbol on the dot matrix (HIGH) or a LED (LOW). IGNITION The warning light is turned on at key on when a signal is received from the NCM SWITCHING OFF The warning light is turned off when a command is received from the MCM or if the NQS is disconnected from the B-CAN network. The symbol is also shown on the dot matrix if a fault is present. Upon receipt of a brake fluid compliant message from the NBC (if the warning light was turned on only for this function). Upon receipt of a EBD system compliant message from the NBC (if the warning light was turned on only for this function). CLOCK/DATE Specifications The clock is shown on DISPLAY (2), i.e. on the segmented LCD display on the LOW version and on the reconfigurable dot matrix display on the HIGH version. In 24h mode, the reading is in hours and minutes and the range is from 0:00 to 23:59 In 12 h mode, the reading is in hours and minutes and the range is from 1:00 to 12:59. The indication AM changes to PM when the clock changes from 11:59 to 12:00 during the day and conversely changes from PM to AM when the clock changes from 11:59 to 12:00 during the night. After each battery connection or processor reset, the clock indicates 0:00 (or 12:00 in 12h mode) and the two points between the hours and minutes flash at a rate of 0.5 Hz - DC 50%. Clock adjustment When the mode key is pressed, the hours/minutes flash at a rate of 0.5 Hz - DC 50% The keys (+ and - ) are used to adjust the hours as follows: Nothing happens when the key is pressed for < 0.05 seconds. The digit changes by 1 step/sec when the key is pressed for > 0.05 sec and < 2 sec The digit changes by 5 step/sec when the key is pressed for > 2 secs and <4 seconds The digit changes by 10 steps/sec when the key is pressed > 4 secs When the 5 or 10 step mode is active, the reading moves on to the next value divisible by 5 or 10 respectively. Press mode is change from hours to minutes. The minutes can be altered using the method used to correct the hours. When the mode key is pressed again, the setting is accepted and the minutes cease flashing. While setting hours/minutes, when the setting is confirmed, the seconds value is restored to zero. During modification, the digits (:) do not flash; the digits (:) begin to flash again when the setting is confirmed. If no key is pressed for 10s during the adjustment stage, the gauge changes to the standard screen without accepting the last setting and then the previous time is displayed. The adjustment keys (Mode, +, -) are not on the panel. The NQS reacts to key depression and not release. The clock can be displayed only with key on. Time setting/adjustment may be carried out only with key on and vehicle speed less than 3 km/h) Clock LOW The 12 h mode is activated only by the supplier and cannot be adjusted by the customer. AM and PM are not indicated in this mode. Press the mode key to enter clock set-up mode. HIGH The 12/24h mode is activated from a menu and thus adjustable by the user. AM and PM are indicated in 12h mode. Press the mode key to enter clock set-up mode. Summer time, Greenwich meantime can be selected from the menu. One hour is added by changing from OFF to ON (Greenich meantime is active). One hour is subtracted by changing from ON to OFF) (summertime is active). Date (only high) The date range is 1999 to 2099. The display format is DD MM The current year is not displayed. Leap years are calculated automatically. Impossible dates are not shown when the date is updated, e.g. the 31st is not shown when the month only has 30 days. Intertia switch activated signal The user is informed if the inertia switch has cut in at each key on. In the LOW version, the FPS on message is displayed in flashing mode - frequency 0.5 Hz d.c. 50 % on (FPS = Fire Prevention System). On the HIGH version, the Inertia switch on + relevant symbol is shown on the matrix display. At key off, the switch status is downloaded for a maximum period of 30 seconds. The NQS makes available the inertia switch on message to all CAN network nodes. OUTDOOR TEMPERATURE READING The outdoor temperature reading is displayed: - LOW version: on the segment display (2) - HIGH version: on the reconfigurable matrix display. The control panel receives temperature information expressed in degrees centigrade from the NBC via the B-CAN network. If the outside temperature is shown on the segment display (2), if the received temperature level is higher, in absolute values, than the value represented by two digits (-99/+99), ± 99°C will be displayed with a plus or minus sign according to the input sign. A "+" sign will not be displayed for a positive temperature. If the temperature is equal to "0", the "-" sign will not be displayed. Some examples are shown below. HIGH version: Screen with TRIP Computer function active - Automatic Transmission (Selespeed) The first screen shows degrees centigrade The second shows degrees Fahrenheit LOW version: The first screen shows degrees centigrade The second shows degrees Fahrenheit Example of error LOW version: If the sensor is faulty, the NQS shows the following message instead of the temperature reading: "--°F" or "-.-°C". HIGH version: If the sensor is faulty, the NQS shows the following message instead of the temperature reading: "---" instead of the units + "F" and "C". Display of "danger of ice" signal Specifications To warn the driver of the possible presence of ice on the road when the measured outdoor temperature is Text = 3 °C, an ice warning cycle is displayed. This mode is run once only after detecting that the outdoor temperature is equal to Text = 3°C and is repeated only when the outdoor temperature reaches + 6°C and then drops to +3°C (hysteresis of 3°C). , the buzzer does not sound again if the temperature does not reach + 6°C and then drops to +3°C. If the outside temperature at key-on is T = 3° C, then the display shows the specified page at key-on for the first 10s and later initiates the "warning cycle". If the "warning cycle" is interrupted by a fault message (greater priority), it is nevertheless resumed at the end of the above fault. Warning cycle LOW version: the temperature reading is shown and flashes for 10 seconds at a rate of Hz, D.C.50% ON; the buzzer produces an Alarm beep 1 acoustic signal. HIGH version the temperature reading is displayed (in flashing mode - frequency of 1Hz d.c. 50% ON) and the message "Snow symbol + warning ice danger" for a time period of 10 seconds; the buzzer produces an Alarm beep 1 signal At the end of the warning cycle: the message disappears, the temperature reading stops flashing, the "snow symbol" is shown in the specially dedicated area of the display (as long as the condition T = 3°C persists) and the screen prior to the anomaly event reappears. The NQS receives and sends an increase signal (CAF+) or decrease signal (CAF-) from a switch on the left keypad to the headlamp adjustment module (integral with the NQS). The adjustment module checks for the presence of a headlamps power supply positive from Fuse F13 and generates an adjustment signal, which it sends to the headlamp alignment motor electronic control circuit. The instrument output signal is a voltage value that is interepreted by the actuator fitted to the headlamp; At KEY OFF, no adjustment is possible. TRIP COMPUTER (PRESENT ONLY ON HIGH VERSION) Specifications The TRIP computer is only on HIGH LINE instrument panels and is used to display trip data on the reconfigurable matrix display. Two separate TRIP modes (A and B) are present. These are activated by a dedicated button in the sequence shown: TRIP A instant fuel consumption Average fuel consumption Range Average speed Trip time Distance travelled TRIP B Average Fuel Consumption - B Average speed - B Trip time - B Distance travelled - B When the TRIP function is activated (transition from INACTIVE to ACTIVE status), the NQS generates acoustic feedback (roger beep). Additional acoustic feedback is generated when the key has been hold down for > 4 seconds to zero the data. Counting/update of TRIP data takes place only with the engine running, i.e. only when the control panel receives a fuel consumption signal from the Engine Control Unit (including cut-off mode, i.e. zero fuel consumption and rpm higher than 300 rpm). The interval between one reset of TRIP data and the next is defined as the mission. This reset may take place as follows: Using the key (pressing for t > 4 secs): resetting by manual reset of one of the TRIP data items automatically resets all the others (apart from RANGE and INSTANTANEOUS FUEL CONSUMPTION). After this, the count for each data item proceeds independently of the rest. Resetting the Main TRIP also resets TRIP B. The reset of TRIP B is independent. The odometer reset (shown as specific segments on the display) does NOT lead to TRIP reset. Automatic: when the distance travelled data item reaches the mileage limit of 4999.9 when the trip time reaches the counter limit of 99.59 every time the battery is reconnected only for TRIP B: when the time elapsed between key-off and the next key-on is greater than two hours. Whenever the battery is connected, all the TRIP values are reset. Measurement unit adjustment via the menu is maintained at all times. At each key-on, the same values displayed at the previous key-off are stored in the memory. A message indicating the active TRIP function is shown on the display Operation The control panel receives the following information to compute these data: Control panel input Received from Instantaneous mileage Body Computer Fuel level (as a percentage of a full tank) Body Computer Fuel reserve level Body Computer Fuel tank capacity Body Computer Vehicle speed Body Computer Instantaneous fuel consumption (litres/hour); Engine management control unit Trip time counted Internal clock The instrument calculates the trip data as follows: Distance travelled The distance travelled by the vehicle from the beginning of the mission is indicated, i.e. since the user reset the counter by pressing the dedicated key. The reading is consistent with the display on the mileometer. When the maximum possible mileage value is reached, the mileage display resets to zero automatically. A total TRIP computer reset is then performed. The mileage reading is displayed with the following characteristics: range between 0-4999.9 km resolution equal to 0.1 km update of display: every 0.1 km - The function is active from key on. Trip time The trip time shows the time elapsed from the start of the mission, i.e. since the user reset the counter by pressing the TRIP key or an automatic reset occurred Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each mission, the display shows "00:00", after which the calculated value is displayed. At each key-on, the value stored at the previous key-off is displayed, except for the TRIP counter that automatically resets after the vehicle is parked for 2 h If the vehicle is parked with the engine off (key off), the accumulated trip counter stops but does not reset to zero. The count resumes as soon as the vehicle sets off again (next key on - engine running). The function is active from key on, with the engine running. The mission time is displayed in hh mm with the following characteristics: range between 00:00 and 99:59 resoluition equal to 1 min. display updated every minute data update every second When the maximum possible value is reached (99.59) the mileage display resets to zero automatically. A total TRIP computer reset is then performed Average speed The average speed is calculated from the beginning of the mission, as a ratio between distance travelled and trip time. Vm = distance travelled/trip time The calculation is performed only with the engine running. Each time the battery is reconnected and at the beginning of each mission, the display shows "----" for the first 10 seconds (10s), after which the calculated value is displayed. At each key-on, the value stored at the previous key-off is stored, except for the TRIP B counter that automatically resets after the vehicle is parked for 2 h. The displayed average speed must be equal to"----", whenever: the user resets the counter by pressing the dedicated button. the distance travelled and/or trip time parameters are reset. The average speed value is displayed with the following specifications: range between 0 - 250 km/h *- resolution equal to 0.1 km/h calculation precision: = 0.1 km/h display updated every 10 s ± 0.1s (10s) Average fuel consumption Average fuel consumption measn the ratio between distance travelled since the start of the mission and number of litres consumed since the start of the mission. Cm = distance travelled/litres of fuel consumed The control panel downloads the fuel consumption signal via the B-CAN network and processes it to divide it by the distance travelled since the start of the mission. At the start of a new mission, due to battery disconnection or TRIP computer reset, the average fuel consumption value is reset to the individual predefined average standard fuel consumption value for the vehicle/engine version. A weighting to be attributed to the above initial value to avoid excessive changes in the reading shown during the first few minutes of the mission. After this, the reading tends to represent the true mission fuel consumption. The value displayed is equal to "----" for the first 10 seconds, after which the figure calculated is displayed. At each key-on, the value stored at the previous key-off is displayed, except for the TRIP counter that automatically resets after the vehicle is parked for 2 h In caso di sosta con motore in moto (semaforo, ecc.) l'aggiornamento del valore di consumo medio visualizzato diventa funzione del consumo istantaneo acquisito, essendo che i km percorsi rimangono fissi (incremento nullo). The value is displayed with the following specifications: risoluzione pari a 0,1 km/l calculation precision: = 0,1 km/l l'aggiornamento su display ogni 10 s ± 0,1s valore max. indicato pari a 50 km/litro - 2 l/100km valore min. indicato pari a 4 km/litro - 25 l/100km Consumo istantaneo Per consumo istantaneo s'intende il valore di litri di carburante consumati dal veicolo nella missione il dato viene calcolato sulla base del segnale di consumo trasmesso dalla centralina controllo motore,. The instrument panel acquires the consumption signal via the B-CAN The value displayed is designed to allow the user to appreciate the differences in consumption linked to the style of driving, When the battery is connected, the value displayed should be equal to "----" for the first 10 seconds, after which the figure calculated is displayed. For the calculation of the instant consumption, in order to avoid the value displayed varying too much, a "predefined average standard consumption" figure is used (personalized for the vehicle/engine type); afterwards the weight of the initial reading gradually becomes less important and the consumption figures are used. Con la vettura in moto ma velocità = 0, il valore visualizzato deve essere pari a "----". The value is displayed with the following specifications: resolution of 0.1 km/l* - calculation precision: = 0.1 km/l *- max reading equal to 50 km/litre - 2 l/100km min reading equal to 4 km/litre - 25 l/100km Range The range indicates the estimated distance (in km or miles) that the car could travel with the fuel currently in the tank, assuming the mission is continued applying the same driving style (same fuel consumption conditions). This value is calculated using information received from: Body Computer: fuel level (as a percentage of a full tank); Engine management control unit: reference fuel consumption calculated by the control unit Value storedi in the instrument panel: fuel tank capacity (litres) Range in km is calculated by multiplying the reference fuel consumption by the number of litres of fuel in the tank or by dividing the litres of fuel present in the tank by average mission fuel consumption. When the battery is connected, the value displayed should be equal to "----" for the first 30 seconds, after which the figure calculated is displayed. At each key on, the value stored at the previous key off is stored. During the mission, the displayed range is updated by amounts proportional to the difference between the displayed value and the calculated value to avoid excessive fluctuations. More specifically: if the difference between the calculated value and the displayed value exceeds 40 km, the change in displayed range is equal to one sixth of the difference. if the difference between the calculated value and the displayed value is between 6 km and 39 km, the change in displayed range is equal to 3 km if the difference between the calculated value and the displayed value is less than 6 km, the change in displayed range is equal to 1 km When the fuel level is on the reserve, i.e. reserve warning light on, and range is lower than 50 km, no more data is transmitted to the user (but the range count continues). In other words, the display shows the message "attention - refuelling necessary" + symbol for 20 s followed by "----" . Even if the trip screen is not active, when the above limit is reached (range lower than 50 km), the message is displayed as described above and then the display returns to the screen active at the time the anomaly event occurred. If the vehicle is refueled, the new range value is immediately displayed. When fuel has been added, if the range is still lower than the required limit (50 km), no reading is displayed and the indication "----" remains. The refuelling information is downloaded as described in the chapter on the fuel level gauge. If the vehicle is at a standstill ( < 3 km/h) with the engine running (e.g. traffic lights - traffic jam), the last value before the vehicle was parked is shown for 3 minutes after which the indication "----" appears. The display is returned to normal operating mode with vehicle speed > 3 km/h. The range value is updated taking into account the fuel consumed while the vehicle is parked, considering driving style prior to the halt (last 5 minutes). The range calculation is always active The range value is displayed with the following specifications: calculation precision: = 1 km) resolution: 1 km display updated every 30 s ± 0.1s max reading equal to 1999 km min indicate value equal to 50 km, after which the following indication is shown "----" Recovery If the computer is not connected to the B-CAN network, all the TRIP counters show the message "not available" instead of a reading together with a description of the data characteristics. If the speed sensors are faulty, all the TRIP counters display dashes "----" together with the data characteristics of each item (km for range , km/h for average speed etc.). If the fuel sensor is faulty, dashes "----" are shown only for Range and Average fuel consumption together with descriptions of each data characteristic. If the fault disappears, the count of the various items continues in their different ways and the values downloaded prior to the mission are not reset and the mission is not restarted. ROBOTISED GEARBOX DISPLAYS (SELESPEED) (PRESENT ONLY ON HIGH VERSION) The NQS receives information on the speed engaged from the NCR (robotised gearbox mode) and displays it on the dot matrix screen as follows: Speed number :1,2,3,4,5,R.N, this information is supplied by the gear engaged signal from the NCR City selection: this information is supplied by the gear change mode signal If this message is not available or if the gearbox is not SELESPEED, the NQS does not display a speed indication. The speed engaged indication is also shown at key off as long as the active matrix display is lit (see paragraph on the matrix display) The number indicating the gear engaged also flashes when the NCR determines that the gear selected by the driver is no longer correct for the vehicle speed, the flashing rate is ± 0.5 Hz with DC 50%. When the message is received (buzzer required), the NQS activates the buzzer with the Beep Alarm 3 sound. ACOUSTIC FUNCTIONS Specifications The NQS contains a buzzer that emits the following acoustic signals. Key operation: roger beep tone to denote operation of one of the passenger compartment keys The NQS receives a roger beep activation signal from the other nodes via the B-CAN network The keys that give rise to the acoustic signal are: front window controls controls on the left keypad controls on the central keypad except the HAZARD key controls on the climate control system Signal for the following alarm types: Alarm beep 1 Alarm beep 2 Alarm beep 3 The NQS manages the type of alarm according to the signals received from: B-CAN network From systems connected directly to the panel From functions inside the panel The NQS generates a corresponding acoustic signal as described below. The buzzer management strategy is as follows: roger-beep: frequency 1.5 kHz, duty cycle 50%, duratation 50ms alarm beep 1: frequency 4 kHz, duty cycle 50%, duratation 2 s - modulation equal to 1Hz dc 70% alarm beep 2: frequency 4 kHz, duty cycle 50%, duration dependent on function - modulation 2Hz dc 50% alarm beep 3: frequency 4 kHz, duty cycle 50%, duratation dependent on function The NQS manages the buzzer activation priorities. The priorities are: Roger Beep: 3 Alarm beep 1 2 Alarm beep 2 1 Alarm beep 3 0 MAXIMUM PRIORITY If several acoustic signals are received simultaneously, only the signal corresponding to the highest priority message must be generated. The others are aborted. Danger signals The danger signals are: If the doors are open and if the vehicle exceeds a speed of 3 km/h for longer than 4 s, the acoustic signal is alarm beep 2 type. if the handbrake is on and if vehicle speed is other than zero for longer than 4 s, an alarm beep 2 signal is generated. If the doors are open and the handbrake is on, the signal is timed (for about 10 seconds) and repeated only at key on When anomaly events occur, an alarm beep 1 alarm signal is generated; If the speed limit set through the menu is exceeded, an alarm beep 1 signal is generated, If the speed limit set for Arabia is exceeded, an alarm beep 3 signal is generated, If the temperature is lower than a set threshold, an alarm beep 1 alarm signal is generated, Adjusting the buzzer volume LOW version: The buzzer volume (for the roger beep function) may be activated or deactivated by pressing the MODE key. HIGH version: The buzzer volume may be set to 4 different levels. Buzzer volume for the roger beep function can be adjusted from 100% to 0% as shown in the table. For the alarm signal, the buzzer volume may be adjusted to a minimum value of 10% as shown in the table, even when the "off" level is selected. SERVICE COMPUTER (PRESENT ONLY ON HIGH VERSION) Display for information for the SERVICE function) When the next service is due, the message "SERVICE DUE IN....." is displayed at key on followed by the number of kilometres in which the service is due (after the initial check procedure lasting 4 s). The procedure is as follows: the message is displayed directly and only at key-on when the kilometre value is less than or equal to 2000 then the message is displayed once only at key on when the mileage value is less than or equal to 1800, 1600, 1400, 1200, 1000, 800, 600, 400, 200 and 100 kilometres respectively the last messages are issued at 50 and 0 kilometres, after which no more messages are displayed even if the driver has not carried out the service. This function can be reset only during technical service by means of a special diagnostic tester. The SERVICE function can be activated only with the vehicle parked (< 3 km/h). RECONFIGURABLE MATRIX DISPLAY (HIGH VERSION) Specifications The display uses a black and white DSTN (Double Layer Twisted Nematic) screen. This particular type of liquid crystal display offers greater contrast and a higher angle of correct viewing than conventional TN LCD displays. Its size is 120x64 pixels The NQS matrix display contains 2 main areas plus a special area for vehicles with the SELESPEED gearbox. It then reappears with the symbol at the next key on for the above time (until the underlying fault is removed). If the fault disappears during the display cycle, the message + symbol are displayed for a minimum time of 2 seconds. The symbol is maintained in the dedicated area (bottom right) of the display and must stay there until the underlying fault cause is resolved. then, when the display cycle is complete, the screen prior to the fault event reappears unless it was displayed in the dedicated area of the display occupied by the fault symbol. It nevertheless reappears at every subsequent key on for the above time until the underlying fault cause is resolved. the navigation system fault prior to the fault event then reappears. The symbol is postioned in the dedicated area for the display of symbols and must stay there until the underlying fault cause is resolved. Display logic with engine running The control panel must detect engine running status as follows for the low battery charge, low engine oil pressure and EOBD fault messages: Engine start-up stage: the instrument panel is enabled to signal the fault message only if the engine rpm exceeds 550 rpm (upper threshold) for at least 1 s (time hysteresis) from the moment this speed level is exceeded. Normal operating condition: the instrument panel is only enabled to signal the fault message if the engine rpm remains above 200 rpm (lower threshold) A = Fault signal validity threshold B = Timer for display of the fault message RPM threshold value Oil pressure warning light 700 EOBD warning light 700 Alternator fault warning light 550 The rpm/reference time values are programmed by the control panel supplier. Led display If fault information is displayed by means of dedicated warning lights on the control panel (not on the matrix display), the message + symbol are always displayed on the reconfigurable LCD display. The written message + symbol remain for 20 seconds and then disappear (both. They reappear at each subsequent key on for the above time until the underlying fault cause has been resolved. If the fault disappears during the display cycle, then led + message + symbol remain for a minimum of 2 seconds and go out later on at the same time. The following faults are considered: engine coolant temperature, low brake fluid level, EBD failure, ABS failure, ASR failure, VDC failure, EBD failure (braking system), EOBD failure (emission control system) DISPLAY LOGIC IF MORE THAN ONE FAULT IS PRESENT SIMULTANEOUSLY If more than one fault is present simultaneously, they are displayed for 5 seconds each in rolling mode. The overall display time is related to the underlying logic and thus they must remain for 20 seconds (per fault) until the message + symbol display cycle has concluded. After this only the symbols will be displayed. If another fault arises during the display of a fault message (message + symbol cycle), the most recent fault supersedes the previous fault only after the latter has been displayed for 2 seconds. The subsequent display mode is still the rolling type described previously (overall time 20 s). If several display cycles are in progress, only screens consisting of message + symbol are displayed in rolling mode. When one of the cycles concludes (after 20 s), the other cycles must also conclude before display of the warning lights alone reappears in rolling mode. If the events do not occur simultaneously, the most recent fault is displayed in the same way as described for display of the first fault, i.e. the message + symbol persist for 20 seconds. After this, the message disappears and the symbol alone remains and the display alternates with the symbols already present in rolling mode (5 seconds each). Example: simultaneous management of 3 faults A - message + symbol B - symbol alone E - event V - display Display priorities First level priority: fault/speed thresholds If faults are present the message + corresponding symbol are always displayed for a time period of 20 seconds If the NAVIGATION SYSTEM function is active: the fault message and navigation system information alternate in rolling mode until the fault warning cycle is complete (total of 20 seconds). Example: 5 seconds. fault, total 5 s 5 seconds. navigation system 5 seconds. fault, total 10 s 5 seconds. navigation system 5 seconds. fault, total 15 s 5 seconds. navigation system 5 seconds. fault, total 20 s navigation system If the navigation system needs to communicate new route changes during the 5 second fault message display, the navigation function display automatically reappears (superseding the fault display after 2 seconds of display time). This display must last for the requird 5 seconds. The warning cycle must proceed to completion. During the display cycle for fault messages lasting 20 s, the MENU (set up) functions cannot be activated (inhibited); all the other functions (activated from the steering wheel or directly from the console) can be activated but no message is shown on the display. The warning message that the SPEED LIMIT has been exceeded is always displayed (with a buzzer). Second level priority: navigation system When the navigation function is activated, the display of all messages corresponding to the functions activated by the centre console (e.g. radio, climate control, telephone, etc.) is inhibited However, the display of messages corresponding to the following functions, which can be activated using the special buttons on the steering wheel, remains activated: If the navigation system needs to communicate new route changes during the display of these messages (lasting 10 s), the navigation function automatically reappears (screen page with pictograms). Third level priority: "various functions (radio....) Commands sent from the steering wheel take priority over those sent from the central console as far as message display is concerned. No priority order applies for the display of messages sent from the same location (all from the console, all from the steering wheel). The strategy is to display the last command issued. FUNCTIONS SELECTABLE/ACTIVATABLE VIA THE MODE KEY Specifications TheMODE, "+" and "-" keys can be used to adjust the panel lighting (dimmer function - see panel lighting paragraph) and activate the vehicle set-up menu. Functions selectable using the MODE key can be activated only with the vehicle parked (0 km/h), apart from the following functions: Panel light adjustment Speed Limit adjustment Set-up menu functions The set up menu mode includes 11 fixed functions and 3 optional functions. For the optional functions, the NQS receives the following information via the B-CAN network: radio present, phone present (NIT), navigation system present (NIT), and automatically configures the MENU (e.g. if no navigation system is present, the function is not displayed) The MENU is updated at each key-on. Display mode Left panel and MODE "+" "-" keys MODE KEY 1 short press (t < 1 s) = Mode1: menu activation and display, if vehicle speed < 3 km/h activation of the Speed Limit function, if vehicle speed > 3 km/h confirmation of the selected function confirmation of the setting/modification and return to themain menu screen (same option) 1 long press (t <>2 s) = Mode2: stores the modifications confirmed by the short press and returns to the standard screen "+" / "-" KEYS: selection of the main functions setting/adjustment of functions in the Speed Limit MENU Dimmer adjustment (if activated with inactive MENU functions) Not all the functions can be activated during the fault message display cycles Example of use of MODE "+" and "-" keys 1 - standard screen 2 - set-up menu screen (choice of functions) 3 - selection keys on left keypad 4 - submenu screen (choice of subfunctions) In detail: The first time the MODE (A) key is pressed (with vehicle speed < 3 km/h), the screen page opens (2) with all the main functions (main menu). The number of functions displayed is lower than the total number of functions, depending on the available display area (e.g. 1 to 5, 2 to 6, 3 to 7 and so on) The current active function is displayed in reverse mode (contrast opposite to that of the other functions). To select the main function required, use the "+" or "-" keys (3) and confirm the choice with the Mode key (D). At this point, the subfunction screen appears and these are displayed in sequential manner. The subfunction screen can contain several subfunctions (e.g. the Clock subfunctions are: Hours and Minutes) To select the required subfunction, always use the "+" or "-" keys (3). Press the MODE key (Mode 1) (C) to confirm the choice and restore the menu screen. After selecting and activating all the required functions by repeating the procedure described for each function, two options are available for returning to the standard screen. The first is activated immediately after selecting/activating the last function considered by simply pressing the MODE key (mode 2) (B) for longer than 2 seconds. The second allows the user to return to the standard screen at any moment provided no operations (selection/activation) are performed for at least 10 seconds (E).
