The operating mode can be changed by diagnostic instrument or the following manual procedure: set the ignition key to Key-On; activate the hazard warning flasher press the rear fog light control button and hold it down using the ignition key, carry out the following sequence in strict order: Key-Off (for less than 2 s), Key-On (for less than 1 s), Key-Off, starting from the Key-On state, always holding down the rear fog light button. at the end of the sequence, the siren emits 5 beeps to indicate the activation of programming. release the rear fog light switch and press it again the same number of times as the desired mode (each press gives a feedback beep) If the button is pressed for an invalid number of times (e.g. greater than the number of available operating modes), the siren emits 5 beeps and is cancelled and the country code is not changed: set the ignition key to the Key-On position within 10 s of the last press on the rear fog light button. the siren emits the same number of beeps as the number which indicates the selected operating mode: each beep lasts 1 s and is followed by a 0.5 s pause. at the end of the beeps, set the key to the Key-Off position: the BC is programmed in the new operating mode. Cancelling the procedure If, during entry of the operating mode, the rear fog lights button is not pressed within an interval of 10 s, the procedure is aborted: in this case the siren emits 5 beeps to warn the operator and the BC maintains the previous operating mode. The market can be changed from 1,2,3,4,5 using the diagnostic instrument or manual procedure. It is not possible to enable/disable the market by setting the value 0 DIAGNOSIS OF EXTERNAL MODULES The BC conducts a diagnosis on the serial line connecting to the siren and external modules, checking whether there is a short circuit to earth or to the battery or an open circuit. The diagnostic check on the serial line is carried out at the time when the communication is activated, typically when the alarm system is switched on. The diagnosis on the external modules is carried out when the system is switched on, by means of the diagnostic commands from which the following information is obtained: There are no diagnostic checks on the perimetral protection switches. Siren: not working (sound transducer faulty) already on (misalignment between BC and siren) does not respond (communication with siren not possible - serial line broken) Ultrasound module: not working does not respond (communication with module not possible - serial line broken) The diagnostic information obtained at the time of switching on is memorised in EEPROM to ensure that system repairs can be carried out. To carry out diagnosis, use the diagnostic equipment supplied. ACTIVE DIAGNOSIS During a diagnosis session, the BC may be asked to carry out a diagnostic check on the external modules: the BC then sends the appropriate command and communicates the result to the diagnostic instrument. If, during this operation, the BC does not manage to communicate with the module, the response to the diagnostic instrument will be: interference on serial line module does not respond Similarly a diagnostic check on the serial line may be requested, which may have the following results: OK, short circuit to earth, short circuit to battery. It is also possible to read the table relating to the alarm causes memorised in the BC. RECOVERY If an external module (ultrasound) is recognised as working, it is excluded for the whole surveillance cycle. When the system is switched on again, the diagnostic check is repeated on the modules which have to be reactivated if recognised as working. Composition The remote control system comprises: transmitter: is built into the key handle, it is on radio frequency and sends a variable code to the receiver. It has two or three function control keys and an LED for checking the transmission of the code and the state of charge of the batteries. receiver: radiofrequency built into the NBC with operating frequency of 433.92 MHz. Memorises up to eight transmitters, and is characterised by a wire aerial which comes out of the BCN and is built into the dashboard wiring The system is based on the transmission and receipt of a radio frequency signal with variable numerical code (Rolling Code). Each transmission generates a variable code, managed by a mathematical algorithm. Transmitter The following figure shows the transmitter. 1 - Lock button 2 - Unlock button 3 - Boot button Specifcations The transmitter is the device which transmits the command code to the receiver; it is built into the key handle Composition The transmitter has a radio frequency stage at 433.92 MHz with range of 20 m. It has 3 buttons and one LED: the buttons activate the control, while the LED visually checks that the transmitter is sending the code and indicates the discharged battery condition. Pressing the buttons can be perceived by the user to allow tactile control of the command received. The position of the buttons is such as to prevent or minimise the risk of involuntary activations (e.g. at the time of key-on). Button operation The remote control has 3 buttons called lock, unlock, boot. LOCK: when the lock button is pressed, the doors are locked. When the button is held down for more than 4 s, the windows are closed and the sunroof is closed (SUPER LOCKING). When the button is released, the movements are interrupted; to resume movement press again for 4 seconds. UNLOCK: when the unlock button is pressed, the doors are unlocked and the courtesy light is switched on. If the button is held down for more than 4 s, the windows and sunroof are opened (SUPER OPENING). When the button is released, the movements are interrupted; to resume movement press again for 4 seconds. BOOT: When the button is pressed, the boot / tailgate is released, visible by it lifting slightly. Receiver Specifcations The receiver is located in the BCN and has a wire aerial which emerges from the body computer. Composition Receiver module with operating frequency 433.92 MHz, and has the following functions: it receives and decodes the signals coming from the transmitter it manages the memorisation of a maximum of 8 transmitters it generates the command for opening and closing the doors (actuating as appropriate the exit from blinker command, if required). it activates and deactivates the alarm system. it generates the command to light up the timed courtesy light. Operating The remote control and receiver system has two operating states: switch on; switch off. Switch on command With the switch-on command, the receiver sends a signal to the BCN which: activates the door locking issues the instruction to change from rest to surveillance to the larm system, in the case of prepared BC. The command to switch on is made by pressing the button on the transmitter: it is indicated by the direction indicators coming on for 2.5 s (the indication is enabled/disabled by EEPROM). Switching on is always inhibited (except in diagnosis) if the key-on +15 signal is present. While the button is being pressed, the flashing frequency of the transmitter LED is 3 Hz. The transmitter makes a complete transmission of the variable code in response to continued pressure on the button lasting at least 50 ms. If the button is held pressed continuously, the transmitter interrupts the transmission after 20 s; to transmit further, release and press again the button on the transmitter. If the receiver recognizes a continuous transmission (code received always the same), after the initial switching of state, it excludes the possibility of a continuous switching of the control. SWITCHING ON The receiver acquires the variable code, compares it with the codes memorised during programming and recognises it as one of those. After recognising the code, the receiver controls the locking of the doors and the change from rest to surveillance of the alarm in the case of prepared BC. In the case of BC with alarm system, if the car has already been locked with the mechanical key, when the transmitter button is activated the BC should activate the door locking/alarm switch-on as follows: Doors locked with key and alarm switched off (auto switch-on time not yet elapsed): no door locking or switching on of the alarm Doors locked with key and alarm switched on (auto switch-on time already elapsed): operation of door locking (opening) and switching off of alarm. Doors unlocked and alarm switched off (auto switch-on time not yet elapsed): operation of door locking (locking) and switching on of alarm. Doors unlocked and alarm switched on (auto switch-on time already elapsed): no operation of door locking and switching off of alarm. The activation of the blinkers indicates the change of state of the door locking in accordance with the figure: A - Locking command B - Locking command with repulsion C - Unlock command Comfort function The comfort function (function present in BCN on request) is obtained by pressing the transmitter button for less than 4 s; after receiving the signal, the receiver transmits a suitable command to the BCN which interprets it as: command to activate the controlled window closing/opening Boot opening function When the boot opening button is opened, the boot may be opened, and the receiver, after recognising the message from the remote control, sends the message to the BCN for: boot unlock switching off of anti-theft protection Deactivation After receiving the switch-off command from the transmitter, the receiver sends a message to te BCN which: instructs the unlocking of the doors permits the change from surveillance/alarm at rest in the case of prepared BC. Switching off is carried out by pressing the button on the transmitter: this is indicated by two flashes of the blinkers at a frequency of 1 Hz, d.c. 50%, (function enabled/disabled by EEPROM). Switching off is also enabled in the presence of the +15 signal. The receiver controls unlocking following the same rules as those described in the switching-on section (obviously only if the lock status is active). The alarm system is also switched off. Transmitter batteries run down information With the switch-off command, the receiver sends the alarm system the batteries discharged status. The transmitter indicates the batteries discharged condition by issuing, when activated, a single flash lasting 200 ms when the button is pressed: the transmitter returns to the normal flashing mode if the battery charge returns to above the pre-established threshold. From the moment the transmitter signals the batteries discharged condition, 100 switch-on / switch-off actuations are guaranteed. The correct indication of the battery status is restored at the 2nd activation of the transmitter after the batteries have been replaced. PROGRAMMING Specifcations The receiver/transmitter system is programmed at the end of the line together with the ALFA CODE. During the car's life, the receiver can be made to learn new transmitters, for example in the case of new keys or cancellation of lost keys. At each new programming procedure, all transmitters not presented during the above-mentioned procedure are eliminated from memory. At each programming, all the available transmitters must be programmed. The transmitters not presented are deleted from memory. Key programming procedure The remote control key programming procedure is managed by the diagnostic equipment and can only be activated by entering the CODE'S ELECTRONIC CODE. The procedure is divided into 2 parts: key learning (during which the secret codes of the keys are received by the BC) and a memorisation (during which the codes received are memorised permanently in the BC's EEPROM memory). Once the procedure is activated, the flow is as follows: the diagnostic instrument instructs the BC to initialise the key learning procedure and gives confirmation to the operator. the operator presses the button on the key to be memorised holding the button down, the operator requests learning: the diagnostic instrument instructs the BC to learn the remote control key. the BC receives the secret code and the ID of the key and learns it. the diagnostic instrument confirms completed learning and the operator releases the button. the previous steps are repeated for each remote control key which has to be learned, up to a maximum of 8 keys. once all the keys have been learned, the operator asks the diagnostic instrument to memorise the keys. the diagnostic instrument instructs the BC to memorise the keys learnt: only the keys learnt during the procedure will be memorised in EEPROM (so all the keys currently memorised are lost and each key not learnt during the procedure will not be memorised). Blinker enablement/disablement Using the diagnostic instrument, blinker enablement/disablement is possible in order to adapt the vehicle to the market where it is sold.

Parking Sensor System The parking sensors provide the driver with information relating to distance when approaching obstacles either in front of or behind the vehicle. This aids parking manoeuvres by identifying obstacles outside the driver's field of view. The information that there is an obstacle and its distance is transmitted to the driver by means of acoustic signals whose frequency depends on the distance from the obstacle. The parking assistance system on the vehicle comprises the following components: an electronic control unit; 4 ultrasound sensors; 1 speaker (buzzer) OPERATION Activation and deactivation of the system The system is activated in the following simultaneous conditions: Key ON Reverse gear engaged When the system is activated the buzzer gives off a signal If obstacles are present, it emits the obstacle distance signals whose frequency increase as the obstacle gets closer. Obstacle distance signal The distance measurements only take place when the system is activated. The control unit processes the information supplied by the 4 sensors, operating the buzzer to signal the presence of any obstacles. The buzzer warns the driver that the vehicle is approaching an obstacle. The tone lasts 75 ms, whilst the interval between the tones is directly proportional to the distance of the obstacle: impulses in rapid succession indicate that the obstacle is very close. A continuous tone indicates that the obstacle is less than 30 cm away. The acoustic signal ceases immediately if the distance of the obstacle increases. The tone cycle remains constant if the distance measured by the centre sensors remains unchanged, whilst if this situation occurs for the side sensors, the signal is interrupted after 3 seconds (for example, to prevent signals in the case of manouevres alongside walls). Rear obstacles are not signalled if there is a trailer or trailer hook. Self-diagnosis The control unit carries out an autodiagnostic test when it is switched on. The sensors are diagnosed each time they are activated. Recovery strategies The sensors and the wiring are continuously diagnosed during the operation of the system. A fault in even only one sensor will inhibit the operation of the entire system. Error signal Any faults/errors are signalled acoustically. The acoustic signalling stops after 3 seconds. Errors/faults are signalled immediately whilst the system is activated. COMPONENT SPECIFICATIONS Parking sensor control unit (cpa) The CPA is an electronic component connected to the rear wiring which carries out functions helping the driver during manoeuvres with reverse gear engaged by detecting any obstacles behind the vehicle. The CPA is connected to the sensors in the rear bumper and to a specific speaker located in the luggage compartment. The CPA carries out the following functions: activating the sensors processing the signals received by the sensors checking the operation of the sensors activating the buzzer managing the diagnostics and the test functions The electronic control unit has a device that provides protection against voltage fluctuations and short circuits Parking control unit. Control unit pinout: CONNECTOR A Pin Signal 1 Ignition-operated supply with reverse gear engaged 2 Buzzer signal (-) 3 n.c. 4 n.c. 5 n.c. 6 Reversing signal 7 n.c. 8 Earth 9 Reversing signal repetition 10 Buzzer (+) 11 n.c. 12 n.c. 13 n.c. 14 n.c. 15 n.c. 16 Earth CONNECTOR B Pin Signal 1 Right interior sensor earth 2 Right interior sensor signal 3 Left interior sensor signal 4 Right exterior sensor signal 5 Left exterior sensor signal 6 Right interior sensor positive 7 Left interior sensor earth 8 Right exterior sensor earth 9 Left exterior sensor earth 10 Left interior sensor positive 11 Right exterior sensor positive 12 Left exterior sensor positive Ultrasound sensors The sensors are ultrasoud transducers working like intelligent transmitters and receivers of ultrasound impulses. Both the impulse frequency and voltage is generated in the transducer. The impulses emitted are reflected by any obstacles; the transducer therefore receives an echo which is amplified and converted into a digital signal and sent to the electronic control unit via the same line used for the transmission request. Each sensor can also be operated as a receiver only, in oder to carry out a triangular measurement between two sensors. This technique allows for improved detection of small obstacles and in situations featuring critical reflections. The sensors all have the same electrical and mechanical properties: the maximum detection distance for each sensor can be adapted using software depending on the location of the actual sensor. Acoustic signaller The acoustic signaller (buzzer) communicates information concerning distance, the activation of the system and any fault. The buzzer is located inside the passenger compartment. The frequency and the volume can be controlled by the control unit.

normal status, with all the functions activated or able to be activated; stand-by, with the functions partly activated and the screen dark System activation The system is activated automatically when the ignition is turned ON and it assumes the status activated before it was switched off last time (normal or stand-by). When the ignition key is turned OFF or removed, the system comes on by pressing the left knob (T16) or the SOS button (T22) for a 'Service Call' (the PIN number must be entered in order to use the telephone). Turning the system off The system switches off automatically when the ignition key is turned to the OFF position. The conditions and functions activated before the system is switched off are memorized and will be restored the next time it is switched on. The switching off is delayed if a phonecall or an emergency call is in progress or if there is a change of language for the voice instructions by about 20 minutes after the call has ended or at the end of the function. If the system has been switched on using the knob (T16) or the button (T22) with the ignition key in the OFF position or extracted, it is switched off by pressing the knob (T16) again or it switches off automatically about 20 minutes later to preserve the battery. Stand-by (dark) Whilst the system is operating with the ignition key inserted, it can be placed in the stand-by mode by pressing the MAIN button (T17) at length. This operating condition (Dark) corresponds to a dark screen with the volume off, but the system continues to work invisibly and therefore the telephone is ready to receive calls. If the limit of an activated function is exceeded in the stand-by mode, a warning is displayed. To return to normal operating conditions, press the MAIN button (T17) or the emergency call button (T22) briefly (the PIN number must be entered in order to use the phone). Volume adjustment To increase the volume: turn knob (T16) clockwise To reduce the volume: turn knob (T16) anticlockwise During adjustment, volume level is shown graphically on the display (this type of display is present only on the main menu for the radio source). The volume of the PTY31 Alarm/Traffic Announcement (TA), phone, phone ringer and voice recognition may be adjusted separately. Automatic volume reset during phone calls During phone calls, the radio volume is reset automatically and the display shows the phone symbol. Mute function (audio volume reset) Hold key (T18) down to deactivate volume of the audio system (Radio, CD, CDC) with any operating mode active (MAIN, NAV, TRIP); the radio thus goes off and the message 'Audio OFF' appears on the display Give key (T18) a short press to turn the radio back on. This reactivates the audio function with the relevant screen. Nav mute function (exclusion of navigation system voice messages) Hold the NAV key down to deactivate the navigation system voice instructions (T20). The volume gradually decreases (Soft Mute function) and the message 'NAV MUTE' appears on the display. Give the NAV key (T20) a long press to deactivate the NAV MUTE function: the volume will gradually increase (Soft Mute function) to the previous setting. With the NAV MUTE function active, all other navigation system functions can be used and the MUTE function will be ignored if traffic information is received with the TA function active or an emergency alarm is received. Soft mute function When the MUTE function (audio system) or NAV MUTE (navigation system) is turned on or off, the volume falls or rises gradually (Soft Mute function). The Soft Mute function is activated when one of the six preselection keys numbered 1 to 6 , key (T13) or key (T15) is pressed to tune the radio stations. Antitheft protection The CONNECT system has an anti-theft protection system based on the exchange of information with the electronic control unit (Body Computer) which prevents it from being used on another vehicle even if it is equipped with a Body Computer. The protection system means that the telematic system cannot be used once it has been extracted from the dashboard and stolen. This 'recognition' procedure is carried out each time the engine is started. This system guarantees maximum security and prevents the secret code having to be entered each time after the radio supply is disconnected (for example when the battery is disconnected). Each time it is reconnected an automatic test procedure is conducted; if the result of the test is positive, the system starts to work, whilst if the codes compared are not the same, the display shows a message on the display which asks the user to enter the 4 digit secret code Entering the secret code The four digit secret code, represented by black asterisks, should be entered using the telephone keypad and confirmed by pressing the knob (R2). The figures entered are shown by red asterisks which replace the black ones. If one of the code digits needs correcting, press the ESC button (T24) briefly to cancel it, then enter the correct digit. Pressing the ESC button (T24) for longer cancels the entire secret code entered. After entering and confirming the secret code, a message appears on the display advising the user that the recognition procedure is in progress. If the outcome of the test is positive, the system starts to work normally, whilst if it is not, the screen for entering the code appears again. The system will not work until the correct code has been entered. The secret code has to be entered for the CONNECT to work after it has been connected to the vehicle's electrical system for the first time or to a different Body Computer from the original one or after a replacement of the system. Personal data If the system fails, it cannot be repaired. Instead the full system must be replaced and this entails the loss of any personal data in the memory. Thermal protection This complex strategy makes use of several sensors. The following functions are disabled/enabled according to passenger compartment interior temperature: up to 75ºC the system works normally, from 75ºC to 85ºC, the volume is limited, the CD player (audio and maps) is disabled and the phone works normally, at 85ºC the phone is disabled, at 90ºC the system is completely disabled. The user must wait for passenger compartment temperature to drop below the limit to resume the interrupted function; this condition is signalled by the message on the display disappearing followed by the function being reactivated. Y. Functions A. Functions active B. Volume reduction from 75°C, audio/map CD deactivated from 75°C, phone deactivated from 85°C C. Self-deactivation Protection against overheating The telematic system components come with an overheating protection function that cuts off operation when the relevant module temperature exceeds a set limit. In this case, the function activated by the module that has reached the temperature limit is deactivated and a message for the user appears on the display. The user must wait for the module temperature to drop below the limit to resume the interrupted function; this condition is signalled by the message on the display disappearing followed by the function being reactivated. Conversely, to exit from the message screen immediately and activate a different function, press the ESC key (T24). The can network The TIN is a+15 node connected to the B-CAN network; this means that at Key OFF, the CONNECT is not connected to the network and cannot be reactivated by the network. The Key On signal is in fact a direct signal to TIN. Information received The information the CONNECT receives from the network is as follows: general information insufficient battery voltage signal switching on of lights key status reverse gear LCD screen brightness vehicle speed current time (hour/min.) right odometer signal left odometer signal set-up information (from instrument panel node) unit of measurement for distances unit of measurement for temperature selected language trip information (from instrument panel node) unit of measurement for fuel consumption instantaneous consumption average consumption current range average speed from reset distance travelled from reset total travel time since reset average speed from time xx:yy distance travelled from time xx:yy total travel time from time xx:yy Information transmitted The information which the CONNECT sends on the network is: Navigation information distance to next manoeuvre pictogram relating to the manoeuvre name of entry channel audio information active audio source (radio,CD,CDChanger) active radio band radio tuner frequency CD track number disc number in CDC RDS string Telephone information Number called or caller and possible associated name in the heading. Presence of SMS message. Incoming call. Navigator set-up information Presence of radio tuner module Presence of GSM module Presence of GPS module Presence of navigator module Presence of Voice Recognition module Languages The languages available for both the strings displayed and the voice navigation messages are: French English Italian Dutch Spanish German The language is selected on NQS which, via the CAN network, informs the CONNECT of the settings entered by the user. Once the Connect has received the command, it automatically updates the new setting. If the voice recognition module is present, the Connect activates a manual setup procedure under the guidance of visual messages. Navigation system (nav) General information The satellite navigation system is activated by pressing the NAV key (T20) which gives access to the main functions. 1 Screen display active 2 Screen layout display 2 Display of pictogram information The navigation system in the CONNECT makes it possible to reach a pre-established destination by means of visual instructions (pictograms/maps) and acoustic instructions. The navigation system is fast, convenient, safe and - above all - very flexible to use because it allows you to call up programmed destinations or reference points such as hotels, places of historical interest, public organisations, fuel stations or Alfa Romeo dealers. The position of the vehicle is determined by means of the GPS (Global Positioning System) on board the vehicle. The GPS system is equipped with an aerial and a receiver module integrated in the telematic system. The system dynamically processes the satellite signals, the signals coming from the milometer, the reversing signal and the information from the gyroscope incorporated in the navigation calculator, integrating them with the current position of the vehicle to produce an 'estimated vehicle point'. This estimated position tends to differ from the current position as a result of sensor imprecision. To correct this error, every 30 metres an algorithm is activated, called Map Matching, which correlates the journey made by the car with the road network present in the map data base. The signals coming from the left and right milometers make it possible to determine the movement of the vehicle and whether it has turned off (identified by the difference travelled between the left and right wheels), whilst the reversing sensor identifies the direction of travel. The Alfa Romeo navigation system helps the driver while driving and advises on the best route to the set destination by means of voice and graphic information. The suggestions given by the navigation system do not release the driver from full responsability for manoeuvres carried out in traffic while driving the car and for respecting the highway code and other traffic regulations. The responsibility for road safety is always expected from the driver of the vehicle. GPS reception is difficult under trees, between high buildings, in multi-storey car parks, in tunnels and anywhere where the satellite aerial reception could be obstructed. If the battery has been disconnected fro the car, the GPS system takes about 15 minutes to become activated. The GPS navigation system takes a few minutes to pinpoint the new car position after it has been turned off and the car driven without the system active (e.g. on a pick-up truck). If there is no satellite information, the on board system uses information from the ABS sensors for an analysis of the data. The GPS satellite aerial should not be covered by metal or damp objects. This car's instantaneous position is identified in the navigation CD-ROM and shown on the display together with the topographical features of the area memorized on the CD. Access to the data on the CD-ROM requires a brief wait whilst the maps are displayed. The system constantly compares the information coming from the wheel sensor, the GPS aerial and the gyroscope in order to automatically compensate for variations in temperature, pressure or any other eventuality which could affect the position reading in any way. The precise autoadjustment of the navigation system requires 50/100 km to be covered after first activation and when the tyres are changed. If the wheel grip conditions are poor (for example slipping on ice), the system will temporarily give an incorrect position reading. During the autoadjustment the position reading is incomplete. The navigation system is completely managed by the telecoms system therefore the only operations which may be necessary are replacing the CD-ROM with one with a map for another area or with an updated map. Internal functions (localisation) The GPS measurements used inside the CONNECT nagivation system are: 1 - Estimated position of the vehicle expressed as Latitude / Longitude Latitude/Longitude values refer to the satellite and are expressed as radiants and Height in metres. The Latitude indicates the reference parallel. Parallel zero is the equator. Car position is therefore defined as the meridian arc between the point of the car and the reference parallel. It is essential to indicate whether the latitude is North or South, i.e. it is necessary to specify the hemisphere within which the car is located: North or South, the maximum value is 90°. The longitude indicates the reference meridian. The zero meridian passes through Greenwich (near London). The car's position is therefore defined as a parallel arc between the car's point and the reference meridian. It is essential to indicate whether the longitude is East or West, the maximum value is 180°. 2 - Vehicle's speed in m/s along the south-north / east-west axes. 3 - PDOP of the GPS point (in actual fact an estimate of the variance on the GPS position error). 4 - Quality data relating to the signal received: (number of satellites, South/North relationship, point in 3D). 5 - Time-fix relating to the last measurement made (makes it possible to identify to which instant the measurement refers). Operating Access is gained to the page with the main navigation functions by pressing the NAV key (T20) briefly with the ignition on. When the NAV key is pressed for longer, the navigation system Mute function is turned on and it does not provide audible instructions any more. When the Mute function is on, the message 'Nav Mute' is shown on the display. Give the NAV key (T20) another long press to deactivate the Mute function. The first time the navigation function screen is called up after each power on, a page is displayed that explains how to use the system. Before continuing to use the system, this must be confirmed by pressing the NAV key (T20) again. This page will not be displayed again as long as the ignition remains on. The following message is displayed on the screen: 'The Alfa Romeo navigation system guides you through the traffic and helps you reach your destination. The highway code in each country must be respected. These take priority over the manoevres indicated by the navigation system. The driver has sole responsibility for driving the car and observing the highway code.'. Screen elements and functions The main informations and functions supplied and managed by the navigation system are as follows: acoustic and visual instructions with indication of distance from destination and estimated time of arrival; Detailed maps in different colours with different scales, two and three-dimenstional perspective, to show the position of the vehicle, the route and the destination clearly; Personalization of the navigation system with the possibility of entering pre-memorized destinations with the name of the road and street number; Automatic storing of the last 8 destinations; Name of the road currently being driven along; Possibility of selecting the route according to one's preferences; Information on current position; Information on journey time; Fault diagnosis of the sysem and warnings about possible problems. If the system contains an incorrect CD-ROM or an audio CD or no CD ihas been inserted, the display invites you to enter a CD whenever the system required a navigation CD-ROM to compute the route or update a map. Navigation functions are managed mainly using the knob: turn the knob to magnify the map to different levels; press the knob to call up the first menu page on the screen; access later menu pages by selecting the 'Other menu' option and confirming using the knob; the menu page disappears when the knob is pressed again. Graphic instructions The manoeuvres to be carried out are displayed on the main navigation function page and the MAIN page (T17) by means of arrows and symbols. The arrow at the bottom represents the next manoeuvre (turn left, turn right, turn around, go straight on or reverse direction) while the arrow or symbol at the top represents the one after that. The number shown under the arrow indicates the car's distance from the turning. The small arrow low down on the right of the display (on the MAIN page) or in the top box (on the main page of the navigation function) indicates the destination direction. The estimated time of arrival and the distance left to travel are also indicated near this arrow. Audible instructions The audible instructions guide you to the destination recommending the manoeuvres to be made and, in particular, the manoeuvre is announced first and then detailed instructions are given. It is possible to have these instructions repeated by pressing the RPT button. Navigation cd-rom drive The navigation system CD-ROM drive is located on the front of the telecoms system and is also used for the audio CD. It is not therefore possible to use the audio player and the navigation system drive simultaneously. The navigation system can, however, operate partially even without the navigation system CD-ROM inserted. In this case, when the key is pressed to expel the CD-ROM with the navigation function activated (so an audio CD can be inserted), one of two things may happen: the system cannot currently compute the required route; the route computed before the navigation system CD-ROM was extracted is still valid. In the first case, the car position alone will be displayed and you will be asked to insert the navigation system CD-ROM. In the second case, the system is able to provide instructions to the destination and asks the user if the guide is to be maintained or not. If the user selects and confirms NO, the system continues as in the first case. If YES is selected, the system stores the relevant part of the map; this operation takes a few instants and the display asks the user to wait. When the CD-ROM is loaded, it is ejected and the system resumes the navigation system function with the maximum scale of '2 km'; in this case, not all the route may be visible. Under these conditions, navigation is limited and and certain functions and commands will not be available. The information shown in the map will also be restricted. When the navigation system is no longer able to continue guiding the driver to the destination, or the car leaves the portion of the map that has been loaded, the display asks the user to load the navigation system CD-ROM. If the user does not insert the CD-ROM the system operates as described in the first case above, i.e. suspending the map information and continuing using GPS information (car location and number of satellites available). When the new CD-ROM is inserted, the system software will automatically be updated with the new maps or new functions. During the operation, a message will be displayed asking the user to wait and at the end the destination memory will be empty. On board (trip) computer To access the on-board computer screen, press the TRIP button (T21). To return to the MAIN screen, press the ESC button (T24). 1 Screen display active 2 Instantaneous fuel consumption 3 Average fuel consumption 4 Range 5 Average speed 6 Distance travelled 7 Journey time 8 Distance to destination 9 Indication of arrival time 10 Parameter reset function The on-board computer provides useful information, some of which is calculated starting at different times according to the type of function: 'From reset' or 'B from hh:mm'. To activate the selected function, select the corresponding icon using knob (R2). When the 'From reset' function is set, the on-board computer provides information relating to the last manual zeroing of the computer. With the 'B from hh:mm' function, the information is determined starting from the last manual zeroing of the computer or automatically from the last time the engine was switched off (ignition key turned to the OFF position) separated from the next starting by a period of at least two hours. The data stored on the on board computer (average speed, distance travelled and journey time) are reset manually using commands on the instrument panel display (see User Handbook). This information also appears on the display (for about 4 seconds) whenever knob (R2) is turned. The parameters of both functions are always available so that the user can move from one to another The following information is available: Instantaneous consumption Average fuel consumption Range Average speed Journey distance Journey time Distance to the destination Arrival time The distance from the destination and the arrival time are available with the navigation system activated. The system stops indicating residual range for values lower than 15 km (dashes are shown instead of the range value in km). In the case of refilling with the fuel warning light on, the system onlyupdates the remaining range figure if, when the refilling takes place, the quantity of fuel in the tank is above about 1/4 of the capacity (18 litres). For lower refuelling values, the range value prior to the refuelling continues to be indicated. 'instant consumption' Indicates vehicle fuel consumption while driving and is therefore useful for showing fuel consumption for the driving style adopted. This value is the same as the two on-board computer functions ('From reset' and 'B da hh:mm'). The value is expressed as l/100 km: litres per 100 kilometres. 'average fuel consumption' Indicates average fuel consumption measured since last refuelling. The value is expressed as l/100 km: litres per 100 kilometres. 'range' Indicates the distance in kilometres the car still has to travel before it will need refuelling. The calculated journey range depends on the amount of fuel still present in the tank and the average fuel consumption. 'average speed' Indicates average car speed calculated from the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer. The value is expressed in 'km/h' (kilometres per hour). 'journey distance' Indicates distance in kilometres travelled by the car since the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer The value is expressed in 'km' (kilometres). 'journey time' Indicates time since the last manual reset ('from reset' function) or automatic reset ('B da hh:mm' function) of on-board computer. The value is expressed in '(h) (m)' (hours and minutes). 'distance to destination' This information, present only when the navigation function is active, indicates distance (in kilometres) between current car position and the set destination. 'arrival time' This information, present only when the navigation function is active, indicates the estimated time at which the set destination will be reached. The time is indicated in 'hh:mm' (hours and minutes). The indicated arrival time is obtained by increasing the remaining journey time by some 30%, calculated on the basis of average speed added to current time. The assistance call menu comprises the following functions: Infomobility (*) Medical assistance ((*) Roadside rescue (*) Personal number Emergency 112 Settings (*) Functions requiring subscription to the 'TARGASYS' service 'infomobility' When the 'Infomobility' function is selected and confirmed using knob (R2), a message is sent to the service provider with an information request. When the provider receives the message, it activates a phone link. When the link is active, the user may ask to forward the information request to the operator. If the telecoms link with the service provider cannot be activated, a warning message appears on the display. The telecoms system attempts to reconnect to the service provider information service in any case. Some information will be sent directly by the operator while other information will be sent via SMS messages that are received regardless of which function is active (MAIN, AUDIO, etc.). The message appears directly above the screen active at the time, inside a window that contains functions 'Save', 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call'. If the 'Save' option is selected, the message will be stored, while if 'Delete' is selected, it will be eliminated from the display and from memory. If 'Map' is selected, the point on the geographical map will be displayed automatically, with the possibility of inserting it as the destination of the navigation system. In this case the message will also be stored automatically. If 'Call' is selected, the telephone number contained in the message will be dialled automatically and the message will be stored. If a message sequence is received, a special window will be opened for each one and it will be possible to carryout the save, delete, display on map or call telephone number operations. All message received will be saved unless they are deleted. The list with all the messages is visible at the bottom of the display, in the main screen of the 'Infomobility' function. Each message is identified by an icon indicating type, date and time sent. To access individual messages in the list, which may contain traffic information, points of interest or weather information, activate the 'Select' function using knob (R2), then turn to scroll through the list of messages (including the part that cannot be seen). When the message you want to read is highlighted, press knob (R2) to display on the screen. An icon with a 'T' identifies messages with traffic information (e.g. accidents). When the message contains geographical information to help locate the point, the options 'Delete' and 'Map' are made available when the display appears. When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays the map that shows the position of the point of interest from the event. An icon with an 'i' identifies messages with information on points of interest or general information. When the message is displayed, the 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call' options are available. When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays a map that shows the position of the point of interest that may also be used as destination or inserted in the system list. With the 'Call' button, when present, a call can be sent directly to the number indicated in the message. The icon with an 'i' also identifies messages with general information (weather conditions, atmospheric events, etc.). When one of these messages, not accompanied by geographical information for location, is displayed, only the 'Delete' option is available, which allows it to be removed from the list permanently. 'medical services' When this function is selected and activated, a medical assistance request message is forwarded - including the car position to enable location by the TARGASYS operator. OPERATING PROBLEMS The CONNECT system is capable of detecting and solving both any faults that are produced inside the system and any overheating problems OPERATING FAULTS: if an internal fault relating to a certain module (audio, telephone, etc.) is identified, the system 'freezes' the last available screen and launches a diagnostic search. The system checks the module involved for a certain length of time to determine the type of fault; if the fault persists when this preset time is exceeded, the best action to solve the problem is implemented (e.g. resetting the hardware for the module involved). PROBLEMS DUE TO OVERHEATING: if the temperature of one of the system hardware modules (audio, telephone, CD player, etc) exceeds the maximum limit, the module will signal that it is overheated; a dedicated warning message will appear on the display. The module concerned will be automatically restricted or disabled. In extreme cases the entire system is automatically shut down until the temperature returns to normal and this will be shown on the display, as illustrated in the diagram. To exit the dialogue window, press the 'ESC' button; the module involved will operate on a restricted basis: Overheating of the 'Audio' module: if the 'Audio' module overheats, the sound volume is automatically restricted irrespective of the audio source activated (radio, CD, CD Changer). A special message for the user will appear on the display. Overheatin of the 'CD Player' module: if the 'CD Player' module overheats, no type of CD can be read: no audio CD can be listened to and the navigation functions cannot be guaranteed (unless the navigationsystem was activated previously without a CD). A special message for the user will appear on the display. Overheating of the 'Telephone' module: if the 'Telephone' module overheats, the module will be deactivated (TEL OFF) with the inhibitaion of the information and service functions (SOS). A special message for the user will appear on the display. System auto-switching off; in the case of extreme overheating, a warning will notify the user that the system auto shut down procedure has begun. When normal temperature operating conditions are resumed, the user can switch the system back on again. Turning the system off There are two different ways of switching the CONNECT system off: switching off independent of the ignition key switching off dependent on the ignition key To make this choice, access the SETUP menu. When the first mode is activated the system can be switched off by pressing knob (R1). When the second mode is activated the system can be switched off by turning the ignition key to the OFF position. With the engine running or the panel on, the system can be switched off by pressing knob (R1). There is a 20 minute delay in switching the system off if there is a destination set or a telephone call is in progress. Antitheft protection The CONNECT is protected against theft and unauthorized systems by means of an 'authentication procedure'. This type of check involves other devices installed on the vehicle including the Body Computer which uses messages exchanged via the telematic network and is activated each time the system is switched on. The procedure is not activated if the CONNECT system is switched on using the knob (R1) or the button (T22) and if the ignition key is in the OFF position. In this case the CONNECT system works normally without carrying out the authentication procedure. Entering the secret code If the ignition is switched ON, the user is asked to enter the 4 digit Master Code to allow access to the standard functions. The Master Code is unique to each CONNECT system and cannot be deleted. To enter the code, a special screen must be accessed. After having entered the code, a second screen indicates that the authetication procedure is in progress. If the correct code has been provided the system is fully enabled; conversely, if an incorrect code has been entered, the screen is cancelled and the previous screen with the words 'The code entered is incorrect' appears. Enter the master code or switch the system off using the ON button. There is no limit to the number of incorrect codes that can be entered. The secret code has to be entered for the CONNECT to work after it has been connected to the vehicle's electrical system for the first time or to a different Body Computer from the original one or after a replacement of the system. The can network The TIN is a+15 node connected to the B-CAN network; this means that at Key OFF, the CONNECT is not connected to the network and cannot be reactivated by the network. Voice controls The user can use the voice recognition function to control the CONNECT by voice in order to carry out certain phone functions. There are two different methods for the voice activation function: with voice identification; without voice identification. In the first case the system is capable of recognizing the command by comparing the voice command with a sample memorized previously. In the second case the system is capable of receiving voice commands irrespective of the voice. Voice recognition and message storage operations are immediately interrupted by an incoming call; In this case, the entire operation must be repeated at the end of the call. The arrival of SMS text messages does not interrupt operations. Voice messages This function allows the user to record and replay six voice messages, in order, with a total maximum duration of 30 seconds for each message. If the memory is full, the oldest message is overwritten. When the time available elapses, the operation ends automatically. The recording activated by the user can last for a maximum of 30 seconds, and is terminated automatically at the end of this available time. However, the user can interrupt it manually. Both the beginning of the recording and the end (either terminated by the user or because the memory has run out), are identified by an appropriate acoustic message (double beep). The Voice Memo allows you to listen to voice messages from the last message recorded and then all previous messages. Once the buffer is full, the messages are played again from the first (in a continuous loop). The Voice Memo allows the entire buffer available for recording to be deleted. Navigation system (nav) General information The navigation system in the CONNECT makes it possible to reach a pre-established destination by means of visual instructions and acoustic instructions. The navigation system is fast, convenient, safe and - above all - very flexible to use because it allows you to call up programmed destinations or reference points such as hotels, places of historical interest, public organisations, fuel stations or Alfa Romeo dealers. The position of the vehicle is determined by means of the GPS (Global Positioning System) on board the vehicle. The GPS system is equipped with an aerial and a receiver module integrated in the telematic system. The system dynamically processes the satellite signals, the signals coming from the milometer, the reversing signal and the information from the gyroscope incorporated in the navigation calculator, integrating them with the current position of the vehicle to produce an 'estimated vehicle point'. This estimated position tends to differ from the current position as a result of sensor imprecision. To correct this error, every 30 metres an algorithm is activated, called Map Matching, which correlates the journey made by the car with the road network present in the map data base. The signals coming from the left and right milometers make it possible to determine the movement of the vehicle and whether it has turned off (identified by the difference travelled between the left and right wheels), whilst the reversing sensor identifies the direction of travel. The Alfa Romeo navigation system helps the driver while driving and advises on the best route to the set destination by means of voice and graphic information. The suggestions given by the navigation system do not release the driver from full responsability for manoeuvres carried out in traffic while driving the car and for respecting the highway code and other traffic regulations. The responsibility for road safety is always expected from the driver of the vehicle. GPS reception is difficult under trees, between high buildings, in multi-storey car parks, in tunnels and anywhere where the satellite aerial reception could be obstructed. If the battery has been disconnected fro the car, the GPS system takes about 15 minutes to become activated. The GPS navigation system takes a few minutes to pinpoint the new car position after it has been turned off and the car driven without the system active (e.g. on a pick-up truck). If there is no satellite information, the on board system uses information from the ABS sensors for an analysis of the data. The GPS satellite aerial should not be covered by metal or damp objects. This car's instantaneous position is identified in the navigation CD-ROM and shown on the display together with the topographical features of the area memorized on the CD. Access to the data on the CD-ROM requires a brief wait whilst the maps are displayed. The system constantly compares the information coming from the milometer, from the reversing sensor, from the GPS aerial and from the gyroscope in order to automatically compensate for variations in temperature, pressure or any other eventuality which could affect the position reading in any way. The precise autoadjustment of the navigation system requires 50/100 km to be covered after first activation and when the tyres are changed. If the wheel grip conditions are poor (for example slipping on ice), the system will temporarily give an incorrect position reading. During the autoadjustment the position reading is incomplete. The navigation system is completely managed by the telecoms system therefore the only operations which may be necessary are replacing the CD-ROM with one with a map for another area or with an updated map. Navigation cd-rom drive The navigation system CD-ROM drive is located on the front of the telecoms system and is also used for the audio CD. It is not therefore possible to use the audio player and the navigation system drive simultaneously. The navigation system can, however, operate partially even without the navigation system CD-ROM inserted. In this case, when the key is pressed to expel the CD-ROM with the navigation function activated (so an audio CD can be inserted), one of two things may happen: the system cannot currently compute the required route; the route computed before the navigation system CD-ROM was extracted is still valid. In the first case, the car position alone will be displayed and you will be asked to insert the navigation system CD-ROM. In the second case, the system is able to provide instructions to the destination and asks the user if the guide is to be maintained or not. If the user selects and confirms NO, the system continues as in the first case. If YES is selected, the system stores the relevant part of the map; this operation takes a few instants and the display asks the user to wait. When the CD-ROM is loaded, it is ejected and the system resumes the navigation system function with the maximum scale of '2 km'; in this case, not all the route may be visible. Under these conditions, navigation is limited and and certain functions and commands will not be available. The information shown in the map will also be restricted. When the navigation system is no longer able to continue guiding the driver to the destination, or the car leaves the portion of the map that has been loaded, the display asks the user to load the navigation system CD-ROM. If the user does not insert the CD-ROM the system operates as described in the first case above, i.e. suspending the map information and continuing using GPS information (car location and number of satellites available). When the new CD-ROM is inserted, the system software will automatically be updated with the new maps or new functions. During the operation, a message will be displayed asking the user to wait and at the end the destination memory will be empty. Operation The satellite navigation system is activated by pressing the NAV key (T20) which gives access to the main functions. The main navigator screen displays the following information: Distance from the destination and arrival time. Navigation information: next turn/type of junction and distance, current position of the vehicle (town, road). GPS signal and GSM signal (intensity of the field). Pressing the right knob (R2) after entering the navigation mode, makes the following functions available: ADDRESS SELECTION: this allows a geographical point to be selected (using an address, place of interest, ...) RG ACTIVATION: activates/deactivates journey driving. If RG is disabled, the voice messages and pictograms of the junctions are no longer available. If a route is activated when the RG is deactivated, it remains visible on the map whilst the new automatic recalculation of the route is not activated. VOLUME: this allows the adjustment of the volume. HOME1/HOME2: this starts the calculation of a route towards one of the two pre-set of habitually used destinations. INFO: this shows information on the GPS position and the route set. DETOUR: this allows the activation of an alternative route. SETTING OF ROUTE: this defines the parameters for calculating the route and allows the activation of the junction zoom. DESTINATION AND ROUTE: this manages the destination and allows the activation of the calculation of the route. VOICE AGENDA: this manages the voice navigation agenda. Use of 'targa sys' connect function When the CONNECT button (T22) is pressed, the service call screen appears. The assistance call menu comprises the following functions: Infomobility (*) Medical assistance (*) Roadside rescue (*) Personal number Emergency 112 Settings (*) Functions requiring subscription to the 'TARGASYS' service 'infomobility' When the 'Infomobility' function is selected and confirmed using knob (R2), a message is sent to the service provider with an information request. When the provider receives the message, it activates a phone link. When the link is active, the user may ask to forward the information request to the operator. If the telecoms link with the service provider cannot be activated, a warning message appears on the display. The telecoms system attempts to reconnect to the service provider information service in any case. Some information will be sent directly by the operator while other information will be sent via SMS messages that are received regardless of which function is active (MAIN, AUDIO, etc.). The message appears directly above the screen active at the time, inside a window that contains functions 'Save', 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call'. If the 'Save' option is selected, the message will be stored, while if 'Delete' is selected, it will be eliminated from the display and from memory. If 'Map' is selected, the point on the geographical map will be displayed automatically, with the possibility of inserting it as the destination of the navigation system. In this case the message will also be stored automatically. If 'Call' is selected, the telephone number contained in the message will be dialled automatically and the message will be stored. If a message sequence is received, a special window will be opened for each one and it will be possible to carryout the save, delete, display on map or call telephone number operations. All message received will be saved unless they are deleted. The list with all the messages is visible at the bottom of the display, in the main screen of the 'Infomobility' function. Each message is identified by an icon indicating type, date and time sent. To access individual messages in the list, which may contain traffic information, points of interest or weather information, activate the 'Select' function using knob (R2), then turn to scroll through the list of messages (including the part that cannot be seen). When the message you want to read is highlighted, press knob (R2) to display on the screen. An icon with a 'T' identifies messages with traffic information (e.g. accidents). When the message contains geographical information to help locate the point, the options 'Delete' and 'Map' are made available when the display appears. When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays the map that shows the position of the point of interest from the event. An icon with an 'i' identifies messages with information on points of interest or general information. When the message is displayed, the 'Delete', 'Map' and 'Call' options are available. When 'Delete' is selected and confirmed, the message is removed from the list permanently, while 'Map' displays a map that shows the position of the point of interest that may also be used as destination or inserted in the system list. With the 'Call' button, when present, a call can be sent directly to the number indicated in the message. The icon with an 'i' also identifies messages with general information (weather conditions, atmospheric events, etc.). When one of these messages, not accompanied by geographical information for location, is displayed, only the 'Delete' option is available, which allows it to be removed from the list permanently. 'medical services' When this function is selected and activated, a medical assistance request message is forwarded - including the car position to enable location by the TARGASYS operator. The message is forwarded after a waiting time of 10 seconds. When Automatic medical assistance is activated by means of the 'Settings' function (described below), the message is sent when the CONNECT key (T22) is pressed with no further need to select a specific function. To prevent accidental call-outs, when Automatic medical assistance is selected, the user is allowed a time of 15 seconds after pressing the key by accident to stop it. All you have to do it turn knob (R2) to another option. The number of the medical assistance centre cannot be set by the user. 'roadside assistance' When this function is selected and activated, after 10 seconds a roadside rescue request message is forwarded - including the car position to enable location by the 'TARGASYS' operator. The number of the roadside rescue centre cannot be set by the user. For both Roadside Rescue and Medical Assistance requests, if the telecom transmission is not successful, the freephone number for the required service will be dialled automatically, to report the need for assistance (the telephone call will only be successful if there is GSM coverage of the area where the car is). 'personal number' When this function is selected and activated, a phone call is automatically forwarded to a number set previously by the user. The setting of this number is described under the next function 'Settings'. 'emergency 112' When this function is selected and activated, a call is sent out directly to the public emergency services. '112' is the emergency services number in all countries where this service is available. A 112 emergency call can always be made even if there is no card in place. OPERATING PROBLEMS The CONNECT system is capable of detecting and solving both any faults that are produced inside the system and any overheating problems OPERATING FAULTS: if an internal fault relating to a certain module (audio, telephone, etc.) is identified, the system 'freezes' the last available screen and launches a diagnostic search. The system checks the module involved for a certain length of time to determine the type of fault; if the fault persists when this preset time is exceeded, the best action to solve the problem is implemented (e.g. resetting the hardware for the module involved). If the system no longer responds to the commands, it can be restarted manually by pressing the TRIP button (T21) 4 times in the space of 3 seconds. PROBLEMS DUE TO OVERHEATING: if the temperature of one of the system hardware modules (audio, telephone, CD player, etc) exceeds the maximum limit, the module will signal that it is overheated; a dedicated warning message will appear on the display. The module concerned will be automatically restricted or disabled. In extreme cases the entire system is automatically shut down until the temperature returns to normal and this will be shown on the display, as illustrated in the diagram. To exit the dialogue window, press the 'ESC' button; the module involved will operate on a restricted basis: Overheating of the 'Audio' module: if the 'Audio' module overheats, the sound volume is automatically restricted irrespective of the audio source activated (radio, CD, CD Changer). A special message for the user will appear on the display. Overheatin of the 'CD Player' module: if the 'CD Player' module overheats, no type of CD can be read: no audio CD can be listened to and the navigation functions cannot be guaranteed (unless the navigationsystem was activated previously without a CD). A special message for the user will appear on the display. Overheating of the 'Telephone' module: if the 'Telephone' module overheats, the module will be deactivated (TEL OFF) with the inhibitaion of the information and service functions (SOS). A special message for the user will appear on the display. System auto-switching off; in the case of extreme overheating, a warning will notify the user that the system auto shut down procedure has begun. When normal temperature operating conditions are resumed, the user can switch the system back on again. INTRODUCTION The style of the car reflects the Alfa Romeo tradition in which all body parts are designed to enhance the car's sporty image. Meanwhile the interor is characterised by soft and harmonious shapes, which create an extremely comfortable environment while retaining a sporty hallmark. Particular attenton has been given to designing the aerodynamics, using guards, designed in a wind tunnel, to shield the rear suspension trailing arms which, together with the profile of the spare wheel compartment, assist air flow along the underbody. Thorough study of space distribution and details has ensured that all possible wind noise has been reduced to a minimum.

SPECIFCATIONS The front doors have been designed with the structure and the panels not featuring any corners to reduce the risk of injury to the occupants. The locks and control levers are protected against break ins by a shield which prevents access to the mechanisms from the outside. The safety lock is activated, from inside the vehicle, by means of a switch in the dashboard. The side panel features an arm-rest made directly out of the panel and an oddments pocket in the lower section and also contains: opening/closing handle; internal door lever; electric controls for opening windows; controls for adjusting exterior rear view mirrors (driver's side only); oddments pocket; The lower part of the panel contains: two speakers, one of which is housed in the door opening lever trim; puddle light; The sliding glass is made from thermal glass and is moved by means of a mechanism with a guided cable. The electronic unit manages the following functions: Single front window opening control; Receipt of window opening button up-down signals from Door Node; Central window opening and closing (with signals received from Door Node); Window anti-crush safety function via Hall effect sensors; Short-drop function on door opening. The up/down commands do reach reach the window opening control unit directly but via the control unit on the door which retransmits them. Short drop Given the particular shape of the door (no upper frame), the correct seal of the door housing is ensures by 'raising' the glass in the seal with the door closed. For this reason the control unit manages the short drop function. when the door is opened the glass, which is in the upper end of travel position, is lowered by about 4 mm; when the door is closed, the glass is completely closed; if there is a control to close the glass with the door open, the travel of the glass stops about 4 mm before the upper end of travel position; and is only completed when the door is closed.
