Control unit pin-out Connector A Pin Signal 1 n.c. 2 Direct supply 3 UP window motor supply output 4 n.c. 5 n.c. 6 n.c. 7 Direct supply 8 DOWN window motor supply output 9 Earth 10 Earth 11 Hall sensors earth 12 Hall sensors supply Connector B Pin Signal 1 Earth 2 Supply controlled by the ignition 3 Hall B sensor input 4 Hall A sensor input 5 n.c. 6 n.c. 7 UP window button input (activated to earth) 8 n.c. 9 n.c. 10 n.c. 11 Door open switch input (activated to earth) 12 DOWN window button input (activated to earth) 13 n.c. 15 n.c. 16 n.c. 17 n.c. 18 n.c. 19 n.c. 20 Ignition-operated supply INT/A PASSENGER SIDE SWITCH The switch controlling the passenger window motor is not an electronic device but a simple control switch with an LED lighting up the ideogram Pin out 1 - Earth 2 - Passenger side window up/down negative signal 3 - Symbol lighting OPERATION ELECTRIC FRONT WINDOWS The control unit controls the operation of the left and right front window motor depending on the installation. The window opening function is only activated if the key is in the ON position, except for the central closing/opening of the windows or the timed delay at the key off. The motor is controlled either manually or automatically, in accordance with the logic described below. Mode is manual when the user starts and stops the system by hand by means of the control buttons. The motor stops when the buttons are released. Mode is automatic when movement is started by pressing the control button for a period in excess of a preset value. In both manual and automatic mode, stopping the windows (switching off the electric supply to the window motor) is determined when the glass reaches the upper or lower end of travel position or through the intervention of the safety system if an obstacle is detected or when the engine is started. This is regulated exclusively by controlling the motor current, which must be self-adaptive, and/or by controlling the information coming from the Hall effect sensors at the motors. the control unit does not download the electric window buttons directly, but via two (UP or DOWN) signals fromt he Door Node (NPG). The control unit must cut off window operation in the following cases: in the end of travel position, in either manual or automatic mode; automatic arrest, after pressing the up or down control again. when the engine is started, except during the lowering of the glass due to the intervention of the anti-crush safety function. In the case of inconsistent commands issued simultaneously, there is no movement. Anti-crush safety function The protection is provided by a check on the torque and current of the motor. For each motor, there are 2 Hall-effect sensors which measure, via the number of pulses over time, the speed of the motor and the position of the glass. The signals coming from the sensors are acquired from the control unit. This function intervenes as follows: the device interrupts the movement of the ascending glass, if an obstacle is present, in time to prevent a force of over 90 N being exerted on the obstacle; Once the protection has inervened, the event is stored in memory. The protection will remain active for at least the next 2 ascents made immediately afterwards. Once the protection has intervened for 3 successive times, the anti-crush function is temporarily inhibited (in order to be able to shut the window in the case of deformation of the door). The anti-crush protection is restored: at the next key-on; following a descent command; after 60 seconds from the last intervention of the anti-crush protection. Short-drop The position of the glass is constantly monitored using the information coming from the Hall effect sensors: When the door is opened, if the glass is in the upper end of travel position, it is lowered automatically (short-drop) for a certain number of impulses until it reaches a 'finishing' position that does not exceed 4 mm. (approx) from the end of travel position. If the glass is already lowered below the finishing position when the door is opened, it should not be lowered further. When the door is closed again, if the glass was closed before the previous opening, the control unit closes the glass until it is in the top end of travel position. If, on the other hand, the glass was open before the opening, the control unit does not do anything at all, keeping the glass open. If a glass closing operation is carried out, with the door open (and the key inserted), the glass stops in the finishing position. When the door is closed again later on, the glass closes until it is in the top end of travel position. The previous considerations are valid if the glass is correctly initialized. If the glass is NOT initialized, or if there is a fault in the snsors, or if there is a 'loss of position', the control unit is unaware of the position of the glass. Therefore, when the door is opened, the glass is automatically lowered for a fixed time of around 300 ms, irrespective of the position it is in. Setting The control unit should be initialized (setting) each time the battery is disconnected. The setting operation is carried out, with the door closed, firstly lowering the glass and then raising it, without interruption, as far as the upper buffer position. CLOSING WINDOWS FROM REMOTE CONTROL UNIT Because the body computer node (NBC) is responsible for managing central closure (AUTO CLOSE) and opening (AUTO OPEN) of the doors, it can also manage opening/closure of the front windows (as well as the electric sunroof and courtesy lights) where this function is available. The remote control unit is equipped with three buttons marked lock, unlock, boot and takes the form of a sending unit built into the key grip. It is fitted with a radio stage (433.92 Mhz) with a range of 20 m. When a button is pressed, a variable code controlled by a mathematical algorithm (rolling code) is sent to a receiver built into the body computer (NBC). This node comes with a wire aerial that emerges and runs into the facia wiring (the aerial plugs into the facia wiring harness by means of a connector and can therefore be changed). The function is active with the ignition key off, provided the window system is equipped with an efficient anticrush seal. DOOR CLOSURE (AUTO CLOSE) - LONG BLINK When the lock button is pressed (single, short press) all the doors are locked and the alarm (if present) is activated. When the button is depressed for longer than 4 seconds (long press), the wndows raise and the sun roof closes. The alarm, if present, is activated. A long pressing action is also referred to as 'super closure'. When the button is released, movement is suspended. Re-depress for 4 seconds to resume movement. DOOR OPENING (AUTO OPEN) - DOUBLE SHORT BLINK When the release button is pressed (single short press), all doors are released and the alarm (if present) is deactivated; the courtesy lights also come on for 15 seconds or until key on. When the button is depressed for longer than 4 seconds (long press), the front windows go down, the sun-roof opens and the alarm, if present, is deactivated. A long press is also referred to as 'super opening' When the button is released, movement is suspended. Re-depress for 4 seconds to resume movement. FRONT PUDDLE LIGHTS When the front doors are opened, the driver and passenger microswitches send a negative signal (earth) to the body computer node (NBC). This wakes up the CAN network and communicates door status to the driver's door node (NPG). The latter switches on the lights in the doors. The function is active with key-off or key on. The connector is fitted with two independent outlets that are shared inside. These control the bulbs in the doors simultaneously. When one of the front doors is opened, the bulbs come on for a maximum time of 3 minutes as a single event. Once the time has elapsed, the puddle lights may be relit only if one of the doors is re-opened. Closure of both doors brings about immediate bulb deactivation. If battery voltage is beneath a 10V threshold, the NPG must not control activation of the puddle lights. DOOR OPEN INDICATION This function is acive only with the key ON Negative signals (earth) from the door and boot open microswitches are sent to the Body Computer Node (NBC) which sends the CAN network input status to the driver's door node (NPG); the instrument panel node (NQS) manages activation of the warning light. DOOR MIRRORS The doors mirrors are moved electrically and heated to demist. This second function is managed by the NBC because the demisting coil is electrically connected to the heated rear window control relay. Mirrors can be moved along the L/R axis and the up/down axis one at a time by means of a joystick and a selection slide with three stable statuses (L) left, central rest position and (R) right. If the selector is moved to the central position during manual movement of a mirror, the current movement must be suspended; the same applies if it is placed in the opposite position (right and left). It is thus necessary to select a mirror firstly and then carry out r/l and up/down movements with the joystick. The control unit should not operate when the buttons are pressed for less than 60 ms. Movement is active with the key ON and maximum duration is 8 seconds. Mirror movement is disabled by: Vbatt = 16 V (re-enabled for Vbatt = 15.5 V) Vbatt = 10 V (re-enabled for Vbatt = 10.5 V) Lack of INT signal (from CAN network) The voltage level (charge status) is present on the CAN network. MANAGING OUTDOOR TEMPERATURE Temperature information is supplied to the network in degrees centigrade (°C). The value to be transmitted (every 500 msecis calculated by means of a special algorithm that takes into account a value downloaded (every 50 ms) from an NTC sensor on the door mirror and appropriately filtered. The information in degrees celcius (°C) is precise to 0.5 °C and is sent via the CAN network for nodes (NCL-NQS-NBC). These users are responsible for applying relevant heating effect strategies: NCL climate control strategies; NQS permanent value display; NBC automatic demist strategies When the battery is disconnected and reconnected, the control unit is able to ensure the CAN network is supplied with the outdoor temperature reading. If the driver's door node (NPG) detects circuit open or short circuit status for 10 seconds, it communicates the anomaly to the users via a special signal. PERMANENT OUTDOOR TEMPERATURE DISPLAY The instrument panel node (NQS) receives outdoor temperature information from the driver's door node (NPG) in the form of a finite magnitude in degrees centigrade. The driver's door node in turn receives the temperature signal from a sensor located on the door mirror. The instrument panel node (NQS) is responsible for displaying the information. If the outdoor temperature sensor fails, the (NQS) replaces the temperature reading with flashing dashes but the '°C' or '°F' indication remains. once 5 seconds has elapsed, the dashes stop flashing and stay on permanently. System operation returns to normal when the fault disappears.

COMPOSITION DOOR LOCK/RELEASE The door catches contain a microshunt and a microswitch fitted to the handles (exterior and interior). These are mechanically connected to the electric motors that operate door lock/release. Lock pin out 1M - motor control from Body Computer 2M - motor control from Body Computer 2d - unlocking signal from microshunt 3d - locking signal from microshunt 4 - earth 6 - from door open signal microshunt Lock control: position of microshunt contacts: from 4 - 2d was previously closed and now opens to 4 - 2d was previously open and now closes. Release control: microshunt contact position: from 4 - 3d was previously closed and now opens to 4 - 2d was previously open and now closes. Door open indicator microswitch on control panel: microswitch contact position: 1st click door open contacts 6 - 4 closed, 2nd click door closed contacts 6 - 4 open. OPERATION Catch lock/release can be controlled by: inserting the key in the front doors using a radio remote control using a dedicated button (with a led) on the facia the button has a single stable status that is activated by controlling: doors locked = led on with key turned ON. doors released = led off with key ON REMOTE CONTROL UNIT The remote control unit comes with three control buttons for lock, release and boot opening. A sending unit built into the key grip (transponder) works at a radio frequency of 433.92 Mhz, with a range of 20 m. When a button is pressed, a variable code controlled by a mathematical algorithm (rolling code) is sent to a receiver built into the body computer (NBC). This node comes with a wire receiving aerial that emerges and runs into the facia wiring (the aerial plugs into the facia wiring harness by means of a connector and can therefore be changed). Door closure lock operation (autoclose) 1 long blink When the lock button is pressed (single, short press) all the doors are locked and the alarm (if present) is activated. Unlocking the doors using the remote control and not opening the flaps, the Body Computer commands the closing of the doors after 2 minutes. Door opening release operation (auto open) double short blink When the release button is pressed (single short press), all doors are released and the alarm (if present) is deactivated; The courtesy lights also come on for 15 seconds or until key on. DOOR AND BOOT OPENING INDICATOR This function is active with the key ON. Negative signals (earth) from the door open switches (front side lights and boot) combine to activate a warning light on the control panel (NQS). In practice, when one or more lines from the above switches are earthed for longer than 50 ms., the body computer that controls the status of these inputs downloads the status and relays it to the CAN network in this case, the instrument panel (NQS) is responsible for processing the information and controlling the warning light DOOR OPEN MICROSWITCH One is present for each door; these are actually the inputs from the control unit (NBC) used also by the door open check, courtesy light and alarm. If one is closed to earth (door open), the doors cannot be locked. REPULSION FUNCTION The lock and release motor control relays are located on the body computer printed circuit (NBC); Action time is 700 ms ± 10%. At the end of this period, the body checks switch position: if they do not tally it emits a repulsion command. The repulsion function takes place following a lock manoeuvre or after a release manoeuvre. In practice, when the motors are controlled to lock and the operation is not carried out correctly (i.e. the controls do not tally), the body orders an opposite manoeuvre in an attempt to realign the catch microswitch contacts. INHIBITION DUE TO A HIGH NUMBER OF MANOEUVRES If 10 or 11 individual open/close manoeuvres are carried out within 25 seconds, the circuit inhibits the door lock/release function for a further 30 s. The last manoevre before inhibition is always a release. After an inhibition period of 30 seconds, the circuit becomes operational if the bar commands are consistent. If the switches are not aligned, the circuit need not carry out any manoeuvres. The switches must be moved once inhibition is complete in order to carry out manoeuvres. BATTERY FLAT If battery voltage is low, and - within 20 ms of the onset of door lock/release manoeuvres - battery voltage (power supply) drops below a threshold of 9V, the device must suspend operation and enter inhibition mode for 30 s. When supply voltage prior to actuation is already lower than 8 V, commands must be ignored. PROTECTION Protection is required for the motors alone in the case of relay binding. No protection is required against motor short circuit to Vbatt and earth because this is provided by the relevant fuse If the fault persists (relay binding), the NBC does not implement any catch lock/release controls and informs the user of the fault. If one of the two connections remains connected to Vbatt (relay with blocked contacts), the microprocessor must activate the other relay to restore the connections to the same potential and deactivate the motor current. The active relay coil continues to use power and can unfortunately drain the battery.

SPECIFICATIONS The tailgate is manufactured using conventional pressing processes and includes large window bonded flush with the tailgate. The edges that overlap the structure are screen-printed in black. The window features a demisting circuit that also includes the area around the third brake light. The tail-gate can be opened: by using the button in the centre of the dashboard; by remote control, via a button on the ignition key. The tail-gate is held in position by two gas struts. SPECIFICATIONS The car features two compartment lids, i.e. the bonnet lid and the fuel filler flap. The bonnet lid consists of an exterior trim assembled on a support frame. Strips of sealant are applied between the trim and the frame. These limit vibrations while also increasing overall rigidity. The fuel filler flap is made out of plastic in the same shade as the body and is moved by hand. A press-fastener is fitted to hold the flap in closed position. BONNET LID The bonnet lid, made through traditional pressing processes, is fitted with a frame with pre-established collapse lines. This safety feature, together with specific retaining hooks, prevent the bonnet going through the windscreen in the case of impact. The bonnet is lined throughout with a preformed panel in sound-absorbent material. This reduces noise emissions to the outside of the car and also to the car interior to increase passenger comfort. To lower aerodynamic noise still further, the front and rear sides of the engine bay are fitted with two seals. Moulded foam blocks are also fitted behind the two hinges. The panel is fastened to the frame by means of press-studs and is made out of compressed textile fibres coated with oil and water-repellent material that is preformed by hot-pressing. The pressing process includes the perimeter finish and holes for fastening. The lid is supported by two hinges, each fitted with a fastening hook made out of the moving part of the hinge. The lid is opened and closed by a single central catch that incorporates a safety hook. The catch is opened by a Bowden cable operated by a lever located in the lower side area of the facia on the driver's side. SPECIFICATIONS The fixed body windows, windscreen and rear side windows are bonded flush with the body. Together with the rear window, they help increase the structural rigidity of the body and increase the level of car safety while greatly reducing aerodynamic noise. WINDSCREEN The windscreen glass is tinted and laminated. It consists of two layers of glass with a sheet of plastic in between. This configuration prevents the glass layers from shattering if struck by stones and pebbles. This maintains visibility and above all ensures a high degree of protection if the window is struck by an occupant's head. The window border that overlaps the body is screen-printed in black. The windscreen is fitted, on some versions, with a rain sensor bonded near the rear view mirror mount base and a demisting sensor located on the base itself a few millimetres away from the windscreen. REARSCREEN The rear window is made out of tempered, not laminated, glass and bonded flush with the tail-gate structure. A set of demisting rheophores on the inner surface of the rear window include the third brake light installation area and the wiper parking area. The rheophore is connected to the electrical system by means of two terminals located on the right and left sides of the rheophore. The rear window border that overlaps the tail-gate structure is screen-printed in black. FIXED SIDE WINDOWS The fixed side windows are made out of tinted tempered glass and bonded flush with the body. A sealing strip on the pillar side of the windows prevents turbulence and wind noise with the door closed. The rear window border that overlaps the tail-gate structure is screen-printed in black.

SPECIFICATIONS All vehicle interior trim is designed to satisfy severe international flame-resistance standards. The main components are slow-burning: they do not ignite due to accidental contact (for example, if a cigarette is dropped), flames do not develop and, in the presence of fierce heat they burn to produce strong, dense smoke. Trim design and configuration is aimed at producing a high level of acoustic comfort combined with a high degree of passive safety. All the protrusions that could harm car occupants in the case of impact have been eliminated. Symbols describing the correct use of the baby seat in the presence of a passenger air bag are shown on the inner side of the passenger side sun visor Characteristic of working principle 5580C AIR BAG SYSTEM . For greater comfort, light bulbs are fitted on either side of the mirrors and on the right and left sun blinds. A courtesy light is fitted in the front of the passenger compartment and another in the rear. The luggage compartment is also fitted with a courtesy light. Puddle lights are housed in the lower rear area of the door panels (for a description of courtesy light operation Characteristic of working principle 7005M FRONT ELECTRIC WINDOWS . PASSENGER COMPARTMENT COURTESY LIGHT SYSTEM Front courtesy light View of front courtesy light A - Left switch B - Right switch The front seats are lit by a courtesy light unit that contains two courtesy lights and a spot lamp, each with its own control switch. The courtesy light comes on for about 3 minutes when the door is opened (provided the door is left open). After this it goes off. If the doors are closed, for a 3 minute period the light is left on for about 7 seconds and then turned off gradually so that the car can be started. When the doors are opened using a remote control, the courtesy light goes on gradually and a timer lasting about 15 seconds activates at the same time. The courtesy light goes off gradually when the doors are locked using a remote control. The light goes off in any case when the ignition key is turned to ON. The courtesy light can be set to three positions by means of switch A (left): switch in central position (1) - both courtesy lights come on when a door is opened; switch moved to the left (0) - both courtesy lights stay off; switch moved to the right (2) - both courtesy lights stay on. The courtesy light may be set to three positions by means of switch B (right): switch moved to the left (1) - left light comes on; switch moved to the right (2) - right light comes on; switch in central position (0) - both lights stay off. Before getting out of the car, ensure that both switches are in central position (0). This ensures that the courtesy lights go off automatically after a few seconds when the doors are closed. Rear courtesy light View of rear courtesy light A - Switch The rear seats are lit by a courtesy light that comes on for about 3 minutes when a door is opened and then goes off gradually. When the doors are closed, the timer of about 7 seconds is activated, as for the front courtesy light, before the light goes off. When the doors are opened using a remote control, the courtesy light goes on gradually and a timer lasting about 15 seconds activates at the same time. The courtesy light goes off gradually when the doors are locked using a remote control. The light goes off in any case when the ignition key is turned to ON. The courtesy light can be set to three positions: switch in central position (0) - the courtesy light comes on automatically when a door is opened; switch moved to the left (1) - the courtesy light stays off; switch moved to the right (2) - the courtesy light stays off. before getting out of the car, ensure that the switch is in central position (0) to ensure the courtesy light goes off after a few seconds when the doors are closed Vanity mirror courtesy light Courtesy lights on the driver and passenger side sun visors come on when the cover is opened regardless of ignition key position. They go off automatically when the cover is closed Puddle light Puddle lights in the doors feature a two-tone lens. The lower part, which lights the ground, is white while the upper warning light part is red. The courtesy lights come on when one of the doors on both sides is opened, regardless of ignition key position. They stay on for about 3 minutes with the door open and then go off gradually. The courtesy lights go off over a 3 minute period when the door is closed. PASSENGER COMPARTMENT LIGHTING Luggage compartment courtesy light The luggage compartment is made easier to use by a courtesy light located on the right wheel arch trim. This lights up automatically when the tail-gate is opend and goes off when it is closed. The courtesy light may be kept off by depressing one of its sides. Glove compartment light The facia glove compartment is fitted with an interior light. The light comes on when the flap is opened and goes off when it is closed.

SPECIFICATIONS The front seats have been designed to optimize comfort and safety and ensure maximum driving comfort, ideal lateral containment properties and lumbar support. The base structure is fastened to the seat lift unit and is made out of pressed steel with an antisubmarining ridge. This prevents the occupant from sliding under the lap part of the seat belt if the car decelerates abruptly. The squab frame is made out of a pressed steel structure that improves energy absorption in the case of rear impact. This is anchored to the seat lift unit by means of a bilateral joint. On three-door versions, the squab can be tilted by means of the release handle, which allows the seat to tilt and glide forward in a single manoeuvre. Subsquent repositioning is aided by a memory mechanism in the slide guides. This allows the seat to be restored to its initial position automatically. Squab rake may be adjusted by turning a knob on the outside near the joint. The squab supports a height-adjustable head restraint. This can be moved through a travel of about 50 mm by means of a release button located on the right side of the head restraint. The seat lift unit consists of a steel frame that includes the lift mechanism. The slide guides are secured to the lift mechanism, cushion and squab. The seat belt branch (fitted with the fastening sensor on the driver's seat) is secured to the inner side of the seat lift unit. Driver's seat reach may be adjusted through a travel of 230 mm along angled guides. Seat ride may be adjusted through a travel of 60 mm by means of a new type of mechanism that moves the seat in an arc (a maximum height movement corresponds to a horizontal forward movement of about 50 mm). This mechanism is operated by a ratchet lever. The driver's seat squab also comes with lumbar adjustment. This is operated by means of a knob on the side facing toward the outside of the car. On certain versions, the seats are also fitted with heating pads located between the trim and padding. The heating is operated by means of a switch on the outer seat trim. On certain versions, an opening arm-rest is fitted between the seats. This is secured to the lower central trim and can be used to stow small items. SPECIFICATIONS The rear seat folds down separately (60% - 40%), with side fillers anchored to the bodywork. The squab has a central armrest which, when lowered, gives access to a flap which communicates with the luggage compartment. This space allows long objects to be transported without having to lower the squab. The rear seats are also fitted with squabs built to ensure maximum occupant safety in the case of various types of impact. They also prevent items in the luggage compartment from being propelled forward. At the base of the squab there are the mountings for the seat belt buckles. At the top of the squab, there is an embellishment for securing the central seat belt section, when not in use. The rear cushions come with a pressed steel base with antislip profile that forms an effective antisubmarining structure in conjunction with the beam welded to the rear floor pan. The rear seat squab can be folded separately 40/60%. This feature is standard on all cars. A fold-down arm-rest is located on the squab between the two side seats. The seats are fitted with two head restraints for the side seats, which can be adjusted to two positions, and a third head restraint for the central seat with the same specifications. Versions with a third head restraint also come with a central inertia reel seat belt. To fold the seat, proceed as follows: Tilt the cushion. Remove the rear head restraints and secure them in their specific seats in the cushion. Operate the side locks and fold down the squab until a single load compartment, comprising the luggage compartment, is obtained. The side locks have a sight check system for checking that the squab is correctly engaged. SPECIFICATIONS The front and rear bumpers are made out of polypropylene and contain two impact absorbing buffers. The wheel arch housings are protected by plastic semirigid plastic shields that protect the inner part of the compartment from external objects and offer partial acoustic insulation while acting as a trim element for visible parts in the wheel arch housing. The lower part of the engine compartment is protected by a cover fixed to the chassis and the bumper and, in the upper section there is a series of covers which can be easily detached for maintenance and repair operations. The other elements (grilles, badges, trims, etc.) are designed to enhance the appearance and spirit of the vehicle. COMPOSITION Absorbent buffers are fitted on all car versions: two on the front strut connection beam and two on the rear trim near the rails. The buffers are made out of expanded polypropylene. This material is resistent to temperature changes, ageing and deformation.

SPECIFICATIONS The car is fitted with seat belts with three anchorage points. As an option, the third rear passenger seat can also be fitted with a belt with automatic inertia reel. The height-adjustable front seat belts are fitted with electrically-operated pretensioners with load limiter. There is a sensor, on the branch anchoring the belt to the driver's seat which warns when the seat belt is not fastened by means of a warning light in the instrument panel (with the ignition ON). The side rear seats are fitted with seat belts with three anchorage points and inertia reel fitted to the roof panel pillars. Standard equipment for the rear seat is a lap belt with two anchorage points without reel. As an option, the car can be fitted with a seat belt with three anchorage points and inertia reel in conjunction with a third head restraint. This device was introduced to increase passive safety and consists of a torsion bar that allows controlled yield during the restraining action in order to modulate the force acting on the shoulders. REAR CENTRAL SEAT BELT REEL The rear central seat belt reel is located inside the squab anchored to the squab structure. To ensure effective operation in safe conditions, the reel is connected via a bowden cable to the squab catch release lever. The belt is free to slide and allow fastening only when the lever is properly closed. A second Bowden cable, also connected to the release lever, locks the backrest by means of a pin which prevents it folding over. The lever is used to release the backrest joint and consequently lock the reel. SPECIFICATIONS The car is fitted with insulating panels to reduce mechanical noise and insulate the passenger compartment against noise deriving from rolling and the external environment. The luggage compartment base houses a spare wheel with tool kit. These are secured in a container which is fastened inside the rim by a device. The spare wheel is covered by a sound-absorbent preformed cover. This is turn is covered by the carpet that lines the luggage compartment floor. VARIOUS BODY INSULATION PANELS The insulation panels are made out of sound-absorbent material secured by bosses or bonded to the body. SPECIFICATIONS The structure of the vehicle has been designed to respond to all situations in an optimum manner guaranteeing a high level of passive safety for the driver and passengers. The parts that protrude from the car's exterior profile, with its flush-fitted windows, and the underbody have been designed with particular attention to lowering resistance of the air to the car's progress and achieving an excellent drag coefficient (Cd = 0.348) and drag coefficient by area (Cd x S = 0.694). These features lower energy consumption and noise levels due to wind noise and turbulence. SAFETY The car body is designed to crumple in controlled fashion in the case of impact from the front, side or rear, or roll-over. It absorbs impact energy without affecting passenger compartment living space by creating a survival chamber that offers effective occupant protection in the case of an accident. TORSIONAL AND FLEXURAL RIGIDITY The body's high torsional and flexural rigidity gives the car good qualities of passive strength while steering is made more precise due to correctly maintained suspension angles to generate a sensation of solidity and comfort while driving. TORSIONAL RIGIDITY DaNm / rad Unadorned body + windscreen 109200 FLEXURAL RIGIDITY DaNm / mm Unadorned body + windscreen 770 These high rigidity levels bring many advantages: lower vibrations; lower noise; increased resistance to failure caused by the use of the vehicle over particularly uneven roads; the sensation of a compact car; maintenance in time of the overall qualities of the vehicle. In the case of operations to the bodyshell, if the structural reinforcements are distorted they must always be replaced. RESISTANCE TO FRONTAL IMPACTS The crumple zone body is fitted with strengthening reinforcements to make the survival chamber stronger. The following main structural changes have been made to meet this requirement: floor pan reinforcements; footboard and dashboard box section reinforcements; rail reinforcements; strut reinforcements; reinforcements on the dome connection beam; pillar reinforcements; suspension attachment reinforcements; addition of bonnet retaining hooks; addition of high strength facia beam in magnesium alloy 1 - Floor pan reinforcements; 2 - Rail reinforcements; 3 - Strut reinforcements; 4 - Footboard and dashboard box section reinforcments; 5 - Front pillar reinforcements; 6 - Suspension attachment reinforcements; 7 - Bonnet retaining hooks; 8 - Facia beam; 9 - Windscreen pillar reinforcements RESISTANCE TO SIDE IMPACTS AND ROLL-OVER To ensure a high safety level in the case of side impacts or roll-over, the reinforcements have been designed to limit survival chamber deformation. The following main structural changes have been made to meet this requirement: reinforcements on the windscreen pillars; reinforcements in the central pillars; reinforcements in the seat belt attachments; reinforcements in the lock striker attachments; beam joining central floor and front reinforcement; beam joining central pillars beneath roof panel. A further important element in resistance to side impacts consists of the doors which are described in the paragraph which follows. 1 - central pillar reinforcements; 2 - reinforcements on the windscreen pillars; 3 - reinforcements on the seat belt attachments; 4 - reinforcements on the lock striker attachments; 5 - beam joining central floor and front reinforcement; 6 - beam joining pillars. STRUCTURE OF THE ROOF The roof structure stiffens the survival chamber assembly in the case of side impact or roll-over. The structure consists of the roof panel in addition to a central hoop, te central connetion hoop, bolted to the side pllars, and a box section hoop connecting the rear pillars. Sections of sealant are applied along the edges of the hoops in contact with the roof panel. These bond parts to confer good mechanical strength while also preventing vibrations and resonance. 1 - Roof panel 2 - Front hoop 3 - Pillar connection hoop 4 - Rear hoop STRUCTURE OF THE DOORS The structure of the doors is of fundamental importance for the safety of the passengers in the case of side impacts and has therefore been designed with optimum geometry and rigidity to keep possible injury of the occupants to a minimum. The structure of the doors includes a side impact bar, waist reinforcement and front pillar reinforcement arranged to allow them to be opened after the most severe frontal and rear impacts. An expandible sealant strip is inserted between the side impact bar and the outer door trim while a heat-moulded sound-proofing panel is bonded to the inside of the trim to damp resonances. 1 - Interior waist reinforcement 2 - Exterior waist reinforcement 3 - Pillar reinforcement 4 - Tubular side impact bar RESISTANCE TO REAR IMPACTS Side impact protection is ensured by rails and connection beams that are welded to the floor pan to create a very strong structure. This structure offers extra protection to the tank, which is secured beneath the floor pan. The rear box section trim and tail-gate ring is also a reinforced area. 1 - Left rail 2 - Right rail 3 - Connection beam 4 - Connection beams 5 - Rear box section trim 6 - Rear floor pan TYPICAL MEASUREMENTS DIAGRAM FOR CHECKING UNDERBODY This chapter contains typical body measurements that may be used by bodyshops to achieve the best results if repairs are necessary. It is possible to carry out a preliminary check to assess the extent of any deformation without removing the mechanical parts. To do this, use a check rod to take measurements at the points indicated in the following figure. Ensure that diagonals B-F / C-E or A -E / B-D are the same (with a tolerance of ± 2 mm). The check operation is completed by restoring the dimensions using the appropriate equipment. This procedure must always be carried out before the damaged panels are repaired and/or replaced. Remember to check mechanical elements which could have suffered deformation. MEASUREMENT POINTS ON THE VEHICLE GAP VALUES MEASUREMENT POINTS ON THE VEHICLE GAP VALUES PREVENTATIVE SAFETY SOUND INSULATION The vehicle is very quiet and the noise level at a speed of 120 km/hour in fifth gear is 70 decibels. Driving comfort (i.e. passenger compartment noise levels and roominess) has been improved mainly by insulating against road surface and mechanical noise by applying heat-expandible soundproofing materials and also taking special care over parts assembly and aerodynamics. The soundproofing materials used to lower noise level are mainly bituminous. Their role is to deaden the noise generated by mechancial vibrations from areas such as the underbody, door interior and external environment. The heat-expandible materials are synthetic rubbers or resins. Their function is to fill in boxed sections to eliminate sound propogation (wind noise). When the body is placed inside the paint-stoving ovens, these materials expand (up to ten times) and vulcanise so that they bond to the inner surfaces of panels with which they come into contact and fill the cavity. A - Sound-insulating materials B - Soundproofing materials C - Sound-deadening materials D - Heat expandible materials D - Preformed synthetic blocks The following measures have been taken to achieve an optimum level of sound insulation: insertion of heat-expandible septa in the rails, windscreen and rear window pillars, central pillars and spoilers; insertion of preformed synthetic blocks into central pillar body nodes to prevent vibrations being transmitted into the passenger compartment; damping lining for panels through application of bituminous heat labile materials before painting; sound-deadening linings for the front of the dashboard, the front and rear running boards, the load platform and side panels with pre-formed, composite panels; sound-absorbent trim for the bonnet and roof; use of double-faced seals in the cable ducting holes between engine bay and passenger compartment; a thorough check of the sealants. All the engines and mechanical components fitted to the car belong to a new generation engineered for improved acoustic/vibrational qualities. Good aerodynamics have been ensured by improving car shape and adjusting the profiles of components that impair acoustic comfort: To maintain the high level of acoustic comfort reached, the vehicle must be restored to its factory configuration in in the case of repairs. BODYSHELL PROTECTION The bodyshell has been designed to be resistant for many years (8 years for perforation, 10 years for structural weakening) to any kind of environmental attacks as far as both the internal parts, which are not visible but potentially subject to corrosion, and the external parts, subject above all to damage which could adversely affect the appearance of the vehicle, are concerned. This result has been achieved by designing the structure of interior panels to limit exposure to corrosive infiltrations and making widespread use of galvanised panels. Galvanising On the vehicle 88% of the bodyshell consists of panels which have been galvanized, divided into 75% twin galvanized panels and 13% single galvanized. Both the outer parts and the moveable parts are made completely from double galvanized panels with the sole exception of the roof which is made from a panel which is not galvanized as it is not very subject to corrosion. Following the galvanizing treatment, the bodyshell is subjected to bonderization, a treatment which washes any grease or surface oxidation from the panels and to painting by cataphoresis, a treatment which is fundamental for protection and subsequent painting. All joints between bodyshell panels are sealed to prevent infiltrations of corrosive agents. Abrasion-proof coatings and protections Once sealants have been applied, abrasion-proof protections are added to body areas exposed to gravel chipping. This protection offers good properties of flexibility and adhesion and also makes a considerable contribution to noise damping. All opening and holes not involved in the fastening of mechanical parts are also closed. Both materials, sealants and anti-abrasives, are then dried in the oven. Areas afected by the application of sealants and vinyl protection Painting The aim of painting is to protect panels and maintain the car's appearance (gloss and richness of colour) The car colour range includes two-coat pastel shades, metallic shades and 3 iridescent shades. The type of colour for the vehicle and its characteristics are indicated on the identification plate which contains the following information: product supplier; enamel colour and type; shade code; type of product to be used for retouches and painting in the case of service operations. MATERIAL RECYCLABILITY MATERIAL RECYCLING Main specifications According to the EEC End Of Life (EOL) directive, a total of 80% of metal and non-metallic parts should be recovered to produce new material and 5% of the remainder should be used for energy production. At present, some 75% of the vehicle consists of metal that can be easily recovered for smelting by using the different metal melting points. All the remaining parts of the vehicle, i.e. some 25% by weight, must be recovered prior to this stage. The problem of recycling plastic materials can be solved from the design; during this stage is it necessary to evaluate the possiblity of reusing the material in future components. The aims to be considered during design include: ease of component disassembly; choice of noble materials in the recyclable polymer chain (with priority given to parts made out of a single family, e.g. PP). Recycling does not allow the same component to be produced as the starting one because the necessary properties of reliability cannot be guaranteed or it may not be suitable. The plastic materials are recycled in a cascade pattern. For example: insulating materials for building are obtained from seat upholstery; the material for wheel arch liners which comes from the bumpers is then used in the next stage for producing sound insulation linings and finally ends up as fuel for the production of energy. This model has been designed so that all the plastic and rubber components weighing more than 50 grams are marked with coded symbols which identify the material for recycling and therefore all the components can be recycled. Recycling therefore involves three successive generations of vehicles, contributing to savings in raw materials. We are currently examining other material recycling chains, including chains unrelated to the automotive industry, following an initiative begun by F.A.Re (Fiat Auto Recycling) during the Eighties and Nineties. Another important point is the use of heavy metals in the automotive industry. The metals in question are hexavalent Chrome (Cr6), Mercury (Hg), Cadmium (Cd) and Lead (Pb). These have been banned (Cr6) or their use is allowed only in minimum quantities and indicated in warning labels or information supplied in vehicle documentation. The tables, in the chapter 'General information and technical data - Operating data' contain the symbols and description for the recyclable materials on the vehicle. This is because in service situations the suitable products are selected and used for internal washing, painting plastic materials, repairs, bonding, etc. The aim is to avoid possible damage with products which are not compatible with one another. In addition, marking makes it possible to select organic materials on the basis of their chemical composition. It is also advisable, in a service situation, to separate materials on the basis of their composition in order to be able to send them off more easily for recycling. When the stalk unit collar is operated with the key turned on, the dipped headlamps do not work. In the case of vehicles with gas discharge headlamps, it is possible that both bulbs and the control units are broken simultaneously. It is fairly improbable that there would be faults in both lamps simultaneously, therefore the possibility of problems with the Body Computer should be considered first. In rare cases there could be simultaneous problems with the bulbs, control units and Body Computer. Results of the tests 1 DIPPED HEADLAMPS RELAY CHECK (POWER CIRCUIT) All OK Problems met Operation Swap the dipped headlamps relay (in the underdashboard junction unit) with the main beam headlamps relay (in the engine compartment junction unit) and check that the dipped headlamps are working properly after the swap Continue to Step 2 The dipped headlamps still do not work even after the swap Continue to Step 3 2 REPLACING MAIN BEAM HEADLAMPS RELAY (POWER CIRCUIT) All OK Problems met Operation Replace the main beam headlamps relay (which, in reality, was the one for the dipped headlamps) and check that the main beam headlamps are working properly End of diagnosis . 3 DIPPED HEADLAMPS RELAY POWER SUPPLY CHECK (POWER CIRCUIT) All OK Problems met Operation Refit the two relays in their original positions. With the ignition ON, check that the dipped headlamps relay is correctly supplied by the battery. Then, connect to the relay power supply from the Body Computer and check that the power supply is sent to the relay when the dipped headlamps are activated. Also check that the electrical connections between the battery and the relay are not faulty See See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS Do not connect the relay Continue to Step 4 No supply from battery Restore the correct supply to the relay. If necessary replace the faulty components (if a fuse is involved, search for the cause of the problem) Supply enablement not provided by the Body Computer Continue to Step 6 Connections faulty Restore the correct connections. See See E2011 DIPPED HEADLAMPS 4 CHECKING WITH DIAGNOSTIC EQUIPMENT All OK Problems met Operation Connect the Examiner to the diagnostic socket. The driver's and passenger's electric windows only work in manual mode; when the control button is pressed for over 300 ms and released, the window does not close automatically, but instead stops. The Driver's Door Node unit is programmed to open and close the driver's window both manually and automatically, while the passenger's window can close only manually, while it can open both manually and automatically. The control unit activates the manual function if the control button is pressed for a period of between 60 and 300 ms (short time), while it actibates the automatic function if the control button is pressed for over 300 ms (long time). With the vehicle moving, the accidental opening of one of the doors or the boot is not indicated by the buzzer. The instrument panel node acquires from the network the signal indicating the status of the door switches or boot and the vehicle speed. If a door or the boot are opened and the vehicle speed is over 4 km/h, an acoustic signal is emitted. Check that the supply voltage to the pump on the pump connector is 12V. Meaure the pump absorption current by positioning the ammeter clip for the Examiner on the pump supply cable (on the fuse box or directly on the pump inlet cable See E5050 DIESEL ENGINES ELECTRONIC MANAGEMENT ) The current measured should be between 2 and 10 Ampere.
Check that the pump absorption is less then 8 Ampere with a supply voltage of 13.5 V. fuel pump fuel filter float-type level gauge diaphragm pressure regulator gauze pre-filter

Start up the engine and keep it idling. Disconnect the phase transformer supply leads. Connect the two transformer terminals to the battery. Check that, with the transformer supplied, the engine revs fall until it almost cuts out. If this takes place it means that both the transformer electromagnet and the tranformer hydraulic actuator are working.

Connect the pressure transducer for the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the return pipe to the tank (1a). Turn the ignition ON. Check that, within 30 seconds, the pressure gauge's reading is less than 1 bar. The fuel pump in the tank stops after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and adjustment screws next to the pressure gauge are open (except those on pipes not connected to the system).

Connect the pressure transducer for the Examiner diagnostic equipment between the diesel filter (1a) and the pressure pump (1b) (connect to the filter outlet). Turn the ignition ON. Check, within 30 seconds, that the pressure gauge's reading is between 2 and 3 bar. The fuel pump in the tank stops after 30 seconds. Make sure that the taps and adjustment screws next to the pressure gauge are open (except those on pipes not connected to the system).

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the fuel injectors. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the fuel injectors. Block the pipe so that no fuel can come out during the test. Turn the ignition key to the start position for 5 seconds and visually inspect that the quantity of recirculation fuel which comes out of the injector connections is more or less the same for all of them, and is very little.

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the fuel injectors. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the fuel injectors. Block the pipe so that no fuel can come out during the test. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment. Display the 'measure diesel pressure and engine rpm' parameters on the parameters screen of the Control Unit Tests. Turn the ignition key to the start (AVV) position for 5 seconds and check that the fuel pressure is over 300 bar with engine speed above 200 rpm.

Fit the connector 1.870.752.000 placing it between the turbocharging sensor and intake chamber. Connect the pressure transducer to the tool. Place the diagnostic instrument in the interior compartment and connect it. Select the 'pressure gauge' instrument on the diagnostic instrument, and set it to acquire data in 'inlet pressure' mode with full scale of 2000 mmHg and time selection 10 seconds. Go out onto the road (observing the legal speed limits) and carry out the following test. On a stretch of motorway, drive the car at 2500 rpm in 4th gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part, excluding the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 - 2080 mbar (1444-1581 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 900-1080 mbar. On a fast non-urban journey, drive the car at 2500 rpm in 3th gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part, excluding the initial peak, the reading should be 1900 - 2080 mbar (1444-1581 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 900-1080 mbar.

Visually inspect that whilst the engine is being started (key in START position) the turbocharger actuator connecting rod (turbine stator vane positioning device) moves by about 10 mm in the direction of the actuator. CHECK USING EXAMINER With the engine switched off, connect connector EX09 with transducer EX06 to the section of pipe between the actuator and the solenoid valve. In the instrument ambient, select the intake pressure measurement pressure gauge. Start the engine and let it idle, then wait until the pressure level stabilizes. The reading must not exceed 450 - 550 mmHg. The graphic acquisition of the pressure can be made by selecting the scale 2000 or 4000 mmHg.

Position the vehicle on a lift. Working via the engine compartment, disconnect the battery. Release the air flow meter hose band and detach it Op. 1056B09 MISURATORE PORTATA ARIA A FILM CALDO (DEBIMETRO) - S.R. Fit buffer C10125 on the hose and secure it using a band. Remove the bolts fixing the catalyzer to the centre silencer. Remove the two bolts for the catalyzer mounting and lower it. Fit the flange C10126. Connect the air intake pipe to the pressure regulator network. Close the regulator tap and calibrate it at a pressure of 0.4 bar. Connect the regulator outlet pipe to buffer C10126. Open the regulator tap. Check for any air seepage through a decrease in pressure. Locate the leaks using special foam.

Disconnect the negative battery terminal Disconnect the negative battery terminal. Disconnect the electrical connection for the upstream Lambda sensor. Check that the heater resistance measured between pins 3 and 4 is between 3.5 and 4.5 Ohm at 20 °C. Disconnect the electrical connection for the upstream Lambda sensor Description Connector - Lambda sensor downstream of the post-converter See K17 LAMBDA SENSOR DOWNSTREAM OF POST-CATALYZER ( ENGINE ) Check that the heater resistance corresponds to the recommended value Measurement Value - Heater resistance (ohm) Pins 3 - 4 at 20°C 4.0 ± 0.5

Disconnect the negative battery terminal. Disconnect the electrical connection for the downstream Lambda sensor. Check that the heater resistance measured between pins 3 and 4 is between 3.5 and 4.5 Ohm at 20 °C.

Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. Display the following in parameter mode: Engine rpm Clutch disc speed Road test the vehicle, at a constant speed (about 30 km/h), without changing gear. Observe the two parameters selected whilst driving Check that there are no significant fluctuations/differences in the clutch speed signal compared with the engine speed.

Wait until the pump goes out (The pump is activated when the driver's door is opened and goes out automatically after a maximum of 30 seconds). Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Make various gear changes with the engine switched off until the pump is activated. Immediately after the pump cuts out, check the level of the hydraulic fluid using the dipstick under the cap for the reservoir. If the fluid level is below the MAX mark, note the amount of fluid required to top up.

Visually inspect the pipes, pump, reservoir, hydraulic unit, engagement/selector actuator, clutch push rod (removing the boot covering it) whilst 50 gear change cycles are carried out from 1st to 5th/R and from 5th/R to 1st (with a frequency of 1 cm every 3-4 secs.).

Check that the bleed screw (under the battery drip tray) is tightened to a torque of 0.35 daNm 0.05 daNm, otherwise, even if the pump is working, the pressure of the oil will never reach the desired value. Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment and take a pressure reading. With the pump switched off, the pressure should be between 40 and 55 bar at ambient temperature.

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. Using the Examiner Plus or Smart, check that the battery voltage is above 11 V; Using the Examiner Plus or Smart, check the pump replay output state (ON/OFF). Make gear changes until the pump is activated. Halt the gear change requests and check how long the electric pump remains activated (listening to the pump and, at the same time, looking at the Examiner Plus or Smart when the 'Pump relay' parameter state changes from ON to OFF). If the battery voltage, at ambient temperature (15-20 °Χ), is more than 11V and the "Pump relay ON" time is betwee 4 and 14 seconds, the pump is working properly. If the battery voltage, at ambient temperature (15-20 °C), is more than 11V and the "Pump relay ON" time is betwee 4 and 14 seconds, the pump is working properly.

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the display of the input state (ON/OFF) for the switch on the brake pedal. Press the brake pedal and check that the value displayed changes (from released to pressed or viceversa).

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the input status display (ON/OFF) for the City button. Press and release the automatic operation button at the bottom of the gear lever (the check is carried out with the engine on). Check that the state has changed using the Examiner. Start up the engine and check that when the button is pressed the word 'CITY' appears on the display.

No accelerator pedal information The signal is received by the Selespeed control unit via the CAN line: Select the CAN information on the Examiner Plus or Smart and check for the presence of any faulty control units Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring for the line, in particular between the faulty control units. Clutch solenoid current Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. 1st/2nd selection solenoid valve Carry out active diagnosis of solenoid valve. If the test is not successful, move on to the next step Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Carry out the active diagnosis of the solenoid valve again. 5th/Reverse selection solenoid valve Carry out active diagnosis of solenoid valve. If the test is not successful, move on to the next step Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Carry out the active diagnosis of the solenoid valve again. Control unit broken error Replace the Selespeed control unit 2127E10 hydraulic speed selection system control unit - r r Lever switches error 0/1/2/3 Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the 'LEVERS STATE' display in the parameters ambient. Make all the selections possible using the buttons on the steering wheel (one at a time) checking that the change in state on the Examiner Plus or Smart is correct; the list of selections to be made is as follows: Lever up (+) (forwards) Lever down (-) (backwards) Lever in neutral (N) Lever in reverse (R) Lever released Control unit earth error Check the state of the tightening of the earths to the bodyshell and the engine. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Microprocessor 2 error Replace the Selespeed control unit 2127E10 hydraulic speed selection system control unit - r r Load relay error This error relates to a control unit supply problem and cannot be attributed to the actual control unit Check the state of the battery. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. In particular check the chain of elements providing the supply for the control unit (wiring, fuses, relays, etc.). Starting enablement relay error The Selespeed control unit provides the earth for the starting relay block; if a short circuit to the battery or an open circuit is diagnosed, the engine cannot be started. If, conversely, a short circuit to earth is detected, the engine can be started without the go ahead from the Selespeed control unit. In any case, the problem lies in the parts of the wiring or in systems that enable starting downstream of the Selespeed control unit. Check the state of the brake switch by carrying out the next steps Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the display of the input state (ON/OFF) for the switch on the brake pedal. Press the brake pedal and check that the value displayed changes. CAN network errors check that the network monitors all the control units (warning: any control unit connected to the CAN could cause network operating problems). the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring involving the CAN line. It is a good idea not to be restricted to a visual inspection of the connection but to carry out a test subjecting it to mechanical stress (pull the wires, twist them, check the stability of the pins, etc.). Odd or even gear engagement (engagement solenoids) Carry out active diagnosis of solenoid valve. If the test is not successful, move on to the next step Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Carry out the active diagnosis of the solenoid valve again. Brake switch The signal is received by the Selespeed control unit via the CAN line and via a wire. Check the state of the brake switch: Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the display of the input state (ON/OFF) for the switch on the brake pedal. Press the brake pedal and check that the value displayed changes (from released to pressed or viceversa). If there is no change of state, check the switch on the brake pedal, its fastening, its positioning, the state of the connections and the wiring. Clutch sensor Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Engagement sensor If this error is present, the gear change is slower than usual because the system operates in recovery mode. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Selector sensor If this error is present, the gear change is slower than usual because the system operates in recovery mode. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Clutch plate speed (this signal is detected by the sensor which reads the speed of the main shaft) Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Engine speed (from wire) Check connection between engine management control unit and the Selespeed control unit is correct because this signal is sent by the engine management control unit via a dedicated wire. Vehicle speed The vehicle speed signal reaches the Selespeed control unit via the CAN from the ABS control unit therefore any missing/faulty signals in the ABS control unit are also reflected in the Selespeed System. Check whether there are faults in the ABS control unit and in the engine management control unit that justify the missing vehicle speed signal. If no faults are detected, use the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipmentr to check whether there are communication problems on the CAN line.

the clutch catching often occurs when the engine is hot. 1. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. 2. Start the vehicle and place the gear lever in neutral 3. With the engine idling, read the clutch plate speed parameter value 4. If the clutch plate speed is above zero then the clutch is being driven In active diagnosis, carry out the calibration of the clutch parameters through the 'clutch self-calibration enablement'. Repeat points 2 to 4. If the fault does not occur, move on to point 5. 5. If the clutch is not catching, let the engine reach operating temperature and heat up the clutch (with the accelerator pedal pressed beyong halfway). Repeat points 1 to 3 If the clutch plate speed is above zero then the clutch is being driven

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment and select the 'LEVER STATUS' display. Make all the selections possible using the gear lever checking that the change in state on the Examiner Plus or Smart is correct; the list of selections to be made is as follows: Lever in neutral (N) (stable position) Lever in reverse (R) (stable position) Lever released (stable position) With the lever in this position (check the state using the Examiner Plus or Smart) the following selections can be accessed: Lever in Up position (+) (forwards) (unstable position) Lever in Down position (-) (backwards) (unstable position) Select the City/Manual mode (unstable position).

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. Check that the clutch position is between 28 and 28.5 mm. To adjust the clutch correctly, the locknut must be loosened and then the push rod adjusted until the reading on the Examiner Plus or Smart indicates a clutch position between 28 and 28.5 mm. The locknut should be tightened to a torque of 0.6 ± 0.05 daNm.

With the ignition switch in the ON position and the brake pedal pressed, engage all the gears using the gear lever and check that the engagement is correct on the display LEVER 1 DISPLAY 1 LEVER 2 DISPLAY 2 LEVER 3 DISPLAY 3 LEVER 4 DISPLAY 4 LEVER 5 DISPLAY 5 LEVER R DISPLAY R

Discharge the vacuum in the servo unit, with the engine stopped, by pressing and releasing the brake pedal repeatedly and vigorously. With the brake pedal pressed, start the engine without accelerating. Check that after a few seconds, the brake pedal advances in accordance with the increase in pressure brought about by the operation of the servo unit. Release the brake pedal and, without further action, turn off the engine. Release the brake pedal and, without further action, turn off the engine.

With the Examiner set to voltmeter function, select 20 volts end of scale and 5 seconds. Connect the black probe to the vehicle earth and the red probe to pin 3 of the mist sensor output signal. Turn the ignition on and press the START button. The signal displayed must be a PWM pulse train with a frequency of 100 hz and a Duty Cycle that varies between 10% and 90% as shown in the attached table. The first 100 sensor output readings must not be considered (1 sec). Pin out: 1. Earth 2. +15 3 Not connected. 4 Signal output PWM% Duty Cycle = T1 / T2 where: T1 = pulse duration T2 = 1/f = 1/100 Hz = Transmission duration T2 = 10msec +- 7% PWM from 20% to 70% This is the normal sensor operating range. Within this range the sensor supplies a PWM signal proportional to the demisting situation at the windscreen. PWM = 10% Indicates internal sensor fault This fault is defined as follows: Sensor self-diagnostics revealed an internal electrical fault PWM = 80% This condition indicates a sensor limit condition. This is defined as follows: The sensor optics are saturated due to excessive direct sunlight. The signal is transmitted as long as the above limit condition persists. PWM = 90% This condition indicates a limit condition or sensor fault. This is defined as one of the following: Sensor optics are saturated due to excessive reflected energy. This may be due to a very high level of misting or an object between the windscreen surface and sensor. Sensor internal temperature reached and exceeded 70°C. The internal process is disabled to avoid damage. A fault signal is transmitted as long as the excess temperature persists. PWM = 0 % and 100% These two statuses will never be transmitted by the sensor. Certain hardware faults may be interpreted by the receiving input stage as PWM signals of 0% or 100%. This is due to the static nature of the signal (microcomputer not processing or under conditions of s.c. to +12V or GND or open circuits). Messages transmitted by PWM 100% - Sensor off or fault in communication or s.c. to +12V 90% - Sensor saturated or blocked or with excess temperature 80% - Sensor faulty or directly radiated by sun 70% - Misting intensity from max to moderate 60% - Misting intensity from moderate to slight 50% - Misting intensity from light to perceptible 40% - Misting intensity slightly visible 30% - Misting intensity not visible to the human eye 20% - Windscreen clean - No misting 10% - Internal sensor fault 0% - Sensor off or fault in communication or short circuit to GND.

With the Examiner set to voltmeter function, select 20 volts full scale deflection and time base 5 seconds. Connect the black Examiner probe to the vehicle earth and the red probe to pin 3 of the sensor output signal. Turn the ignition ON. Wait for 36 seconds for the sensor to warm up Spray the gas in the aerosol ( Part no. 71715571) within 60 seconds Press the START button. The signal displayed must be a PWM pulse train with a frequency of 5 Hz and a Duty Cycle between 20 and 60 % as shown in the attached table. PWM% Duty Cycle = T1/T2 where: T1 = pulse duration T2 = 1/f = 1/5 Hz = Transmission duration Pin out: 1. +CH/15 2. Earth 3. Output signal 4 Not connected. PWM signal significance 0% signal line short circuit to earth 20% unpolluted air circulation 40% pollution level 1 50% pollution level 2 60% pollution level 3 80% sensor error 100% short circuit +12 of signal line

Prepare the diagnostic equipment for a voltage graph assimilation. Select the "VOLTMETER" function from the "INSTRUMENT" menu with the time set at 5 seconds. Disconnect the connector for the control unit side sensor wiring and leave it disconnected. Connect the sensor side connector to isolator AD 233 N° 180.63.87.000. Connect it to the probes between pins 1 and 2 of the isolator. Press the START button on the diagnostic equipment to begin creating a graph assimilation. Let the engine run for at least 5 seconds and check that the amplitude signal is more than 1.5 V and conforms as in the graph.

Start the engine Disconnect the battery negative terminal Activate side lights, low beams, high beams, hazard lights, rear fog lamps, windscreen wiper, passenger compartment ventilation and any other in-car electrical device. The aim of activating all these devices is to see whether the car keeps running without any current supply from the battery. Wait a few seconds to see whether the vehicle keeps running. If the engine stalls, this means that the alternator is not operating correctly and the electrical system is not able to keep the various electrical devices in operation without any current contribution from the battery.

Disconnect the 10-way connector from the headlamp, switch on the dipped headlamps and check that there is battery voltage between pin 1 (+) and pin 5 (-) and that the polarity is correct. Check the continuity of the wiring between pins 9 and 10 of the headlamp alignment control unit and pins 1 and 5 respectively for the front and rear geometry sensors. Check the continuity between pins 11 and 12 of the control unit and pin 4 of the front and rear geometry sensors.

Check the continuity of the line for the signal for the rear geometry sensor from pin 12 of the control unit to pin 4 of the geometry sensor Check that the supply lead (+5V) for the front and rear sensors (from pin 9 of the control unit to pin 5 of the geometry sensors) is not short circuited to the +12V or to earth Check that the supply lead (-) for the front and rear sensors is insulated to 12V - Check the continuity of the supply lead (+) for the rear sensor (from pin 9 of the control unit to pin 5 of the sensor). Check the insulation to 12 V or the earth of the clock spring lead Check the contintuity of the clock spring lead in the joint section to the two headlamp alignment motors Check the insulation of the supply lead (+) to earth (pin 6 headlamp alignment control unit) Check the continuity of the wiring between the headlamp alignment motors and the headlamp alignment correction control unit
Check the insulation to 12 V or the earth of the 'sense' lead Check the contintuity of the 'sense' lead in the joint section to the two headlamp alignment motors

Check the continuity of the signal for the front headlamp alignment sensor Check that the cable is insulated for 12 V or earth or at the + of the actual sensor power supply Switch on the side lights and check the supply voltage of 12 V between pin 14 (earth) and pin 6 (+) of the headlamp alignment correction control unit Check that the supply for the front alignment sensor is correct at pin 1 (earth) and pin 5 (+5V)

Check that the connector is correctly inserted in the headlamp alignment control unit Check that the earth supply at pin 14 of the headlamp alignment correction control unit is correct Switch on the side lights and check the supply voltage (+12V) at pin 6 of the headlamp alignment correction control unit
